Subjective
Binance Square — Trump, Xi and Putin Promise More Fuel, but Oil Markets Barely Move

The account carries the market’s answer to the declaration: the three leaders pledged to increase global supplies of refined petroleum products, but oil prices barely moved on Thursday, Brent rising 0.18 percent and American crude 0.15 percent; the joint declaration called for more diesel and gasoline but set no production targets, delivery dates or distribution details; and American diesel still costs around $5.96 a gallon, down 32 cents since the October 9 announcement and roughly 58 percent higher than a year ago, according to AAA.

Subjective
ZeroHedge — IRGC Says 3 More Tankers On Fire After Ignoring Warnings In Hormuz Area

The account carries the evening claim: the Guards claimed three more oil tankers caught fire after hitting mines east of the Strait of Hormuz, having ignored warnings from its naval forces as they navigated restricted areas with navigation systems disabled; the Tara Gas crew abandoning ship after the vessel was hit for a second time in two days, with one Indian sailor still missing; India’s statement that of the 24 Indian crew, 21 were brought ashore at Khasab, two admitted to hospital and one remains missing; and Fars News Agency claiming three “offending tankers” caught fire, at least one after hitting a naval mine.

Subjective
Assafina — Oman Rescues 24 Crew After Tanker Attack

The account carries the rescue: the crew of the Panama-flagged Tara Gas liquefied petroleum gas tanker abandoned ship on Tuesday after the vessel was struck by a projectile while sailing through the Strait of Hormuz; Oman evacuated 24 crew members about two nautical miles off the Musandam Peninsula after the ship caught fire; India’s external affairs ministry confirmed the attack on November 16, with two of the 24 Indian crew admitted to hospital in Khasab; and the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations agency said the crew of a tanker passing through the strait was unaccounted for after it was attacked for a second time north of Khasab.

Subjective
National Security Journal — India Just Got Pulled Into the Hormuz Crisis: 24 of Its Sailors Were on a Gas Tanker Struck Twice and Forced to Abandon Ship

The account carries the ship’s file in full: the Tara Gas was struck twice on Monday and Tuesday in the Strait of Hormuz, 24 of 25 crew rescued, 21 Indian seafarers ashore at Khasab, two in hospital and one still missing; searches continued on Wednesday to locate the missing seafarer and officials in Oman were still trying to put out the fire; the first strike hit the engine room about seven nautical miles north of Khasab; and a separate vessel linked to ADNOC Logistics & Services was targeted on Tuesday, leaving 11 injured and one missing.

Subjective
Kuwait Up2Date — Iran Attacks Ali Al Salem Base in Kuwait: What We Know

The account carries Wednesday’s attack on the Ali Al Salem air base: Iran fired drones and missiles at the base and at targets in Bahrain early on Wednesday; Kuwait’s military said its air defences intercepted the drones, with no damage reported so far; Kuwait’s foreign ministry called the attack criminal and said it threatens the country’s security and stability; and an Associated Press analysis found Ali Al Salem has been struck at least 30 times since the war began, damaging or destroying at least 15 aircraft hangars, several warehouses and 10 buildings near a residential area.

Subjective
Global Pulse 62 — Iran Attacks Kuwait and Bahrain Again as Gulf Crisis Widens

The account carries Wednesday’s widening: Iran’s military said its drones targeted Patriot air defence systems and missile and drone launch platforms at Ali Al-Salem Air Base in Kuwait; Kuwait’s army said its air defences responded to the drone threat; Bahrain said it intercepted a further wave of Iranian attacks early on Wednesday, its fourth in six days; and a tanker was struck by an unknown projectile in its engine room about six nautical miles north of Khasab, Oman, at 4:45 p.m. UTC on Wednesday, November 18.

Subjective
Trending Keywords — Trending Searches in France Today: Strike Turnout Falls as Retirees Prepare to March

The account carries the week’s counts and the day ahead: the interior ministry counted 146,000 people at Tuesday’s protests, including 28,000 in Paris, against more than 500,000 in the unions’ count; union representatives were due to meet Prime Minister Lecornu, who holds talks with political parties about the protests on Thursday; retirees plan to march in Paris on Thursday; and coordinated cost-of-living demonstrations are called in seven European countries for November 20, 21 and 22.

Subjective
Map News — Paris & France Riots Map 2026: Protest Damage, Curfews and Bans

The account carries Thursday’s announced march: from 1100 to 1630 Paris time, from the Gare Montparnasse forecourt to Place Vauban, gathering from 11 a.m., a press conference at 12:30 p.m., the march departing by 1:30 p.m. and ending around 4:30 p.m.; called by the retirees’ inter-union, the Group of Nine; and the Senate due to debate the police bill on November 19, which would give officers a presumption of legitimate self-defence when they use firearms.

Subjective
Brotherhood Herald — Sánchez and Feijóo Face Off Tonight in the Only Head-to-Head Debate Before the November 29 Elections

The account carries tonight’s debate: Mr. Sánchez and Mr. Feijóo face each other at 10 p.m. in the only debate between the two leading candidates before the general elections on November 29, organised by the Television Academy and moderated by its president, Ms. Casado, at Studio A of Madrid Content City in Tres Cantos, lasting about two hours; and the latest 40dB tracking giving the Popular Party 32.4 percent against 30.4 for the Socialists, with the Popular Party–Vox bloc at 192 seats.

Subjective
El Constitucional — When Is the Electoral Debate Between Pedro Sánchez and Alberto Núñez Feijóo

The account carries the debate’s order: the encounter begins at 10 p.m. on Thursday, November 19, and is expected to last until midnight, with two three-minute commercial breaks; Mr. Feijóo will open the debate and Mr. Sánchez will have the last word, as decided by draw; and the five blocks run housing, the economy and taxation, social policy and public services, fighting corruption and democratic regeneration, and migration and foreign policy.

Subjective
Demócrata — General Election Poll: Vox Loses Four Seats and PP and PSOE Advance, According to 40dB Tracking

The account carries the November 18 instalment of the 40dB tracking for El País and Cadena SER: the Popular Party at 131 seats and the Socialists at 122, with Vox at 55; the Popular Party at 32.2 percent and the Socialists at 30.7; Mr. Sánchez remaining the preferred candidate to lead the government, ten points ahead of Mr. Feijóo; and the fieldwork, 2,000 online interviews from November 13 to 17, with a margin of error of 2.2 percent.

Subjective
Demócrata — Montero Attacks Face-to-Face Sánchez-Feijóo

The account carries the objection to tonight’s format: the Podemos candidate, Ms. Montero, described the head-to-head debate between Mr. Sánchez and Mr. Feijóo as “blackmail of the useful vote” and said neither of the blocs they head has any intention of making access to housing cheaper; and the survey of surveys at November 19, across 17 institutes, at 31.3 percent for the Popular Party, 27.5 for the Socialists and 19.0 for Vox.

entry.title: The Bilaterals Are Done in Shenzhen and the Three-Way Room Still Waits, Taiwan Falls 4.4 Percent and Draws Short-Selling Curbs, and Tehran Claims Three More Tankers on Mines East of Hormuz With None Named
entry.summary: Shenzhen's bilaterals are done and the trilateral still waits, Taiwan falls 4.4 percent and draws short-selling curbs, and Tehran claims three more tankers on mines east of Hormuz with none named.
entry.content:
The Night File — The Desk’s Report

Objective

The Bilaterals Are Done in Shenzhen and the Three-Way Room Still Waits, Taiwan Falls 4.4 Percent and Draws Short-Selling Curbs, and Tehran Claims Three More Tankers on Mines East of Hormuz With None Named

The night file: two bilaterals held in Shenzhen and the three-way room still ahead of them; a Hormuz sentence spoken in one of them and carried on one wire chain; a 4.4 percent fall in Taipei answered the same day with curbs on short selling; three more tankers claimed on mines east of the strait, unnamed and unconfirmed; a ratings outlook lowered in New York; and, in Washington's morning, a retailer's report, a claims print and a first trade still to come.

By Eunice, the desk · Collected and analyzed at 0400 ET, Thursday, November 19, 2026. This edition continues the file from Edition No. 62, the Midnight Watch, collected at 0000 today, from Edition No. 61, the Evening Watch, collected at 1800 on Wednesday, from Edition No. 60, the Midday Watch, collected at 1200 on Wednesday, and from Edition No. 59, the Morning Watch, collected at 1006 on Wednesday. Those editions stand unrevised, as a log stands. Where the overnight figures differ from the earlier figures, the difference is stated here, in the open.

The Night in Brief: Two Bilaterals Held, a Benchmark Down 4.4 Percent, and Three Tankers Claimed

The night ran its two Shenzhen bilaterals and left the three-way room still waiting, sold Taiwan down 4.4 percent into a regulator’s curbs, and added three unnamed tankers to Tehran’s mine arithmetic. The President and President Xi held their bilateral meeting at the Kylin Villa in Shenzhen on Thursday and the President and President Putin held a one-on-one there, in the summit account filed below; the formal trilateral session stood scheduled for later on Thursday, and no agreement or joint statement had been reported by midday in Shenzhen, in the same account. Taiwan’s benchmark closed down 4.4 percent and its financial regulator announced new short-selling curbs on Thursday, in the wire account filed below. Iran’s army said three more oil tankers caught fire after striking naval mines east of the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday evening, in the army’s account filed below; no vessel was named in the claim, and no party not making it has confirmed it. The desk takes the files in that order.

What the night settled is the bilaterals, Taiwan’s close and its curbs, and a ratings outlook in New York. What it left open is the rest of the file: the trilateral and its statement, the fire and the missing man in the strait, the radar in Bahrain, and everything Thursday in Washington still holds—a retailer’s report at 0600 Central, claims at 0830 Eastern, and a first trade on the Nasdaq.

Shenzhen at 0400: A Plenary Opened, Two Bilaterals Held, a Hormuz Consensus Claimed on One Wire Chain, and the Trilateral Still Ahead

Thursday in Shenzhen opened in the plenary hall. President Xi opened the APEC leaders’ meeting on Thursday morning and pledged $20 million to support practical cooperation among the member economies, setting out a programme of economy and trade, connectivity, innovation and development, in the pledge account filed below; the plenary began just before 10:00 local time, the leaders posing for a group photograph before taking their seats, in the opening account filed below. President Putin’s plenary words, carried by TASS in the live coverage the summit account draws on, were that the Western sanctions imposed over the invasion of Ukraine had “failed” and that the need was for “unity rather than division, and dialogue rather than ultimatums,” in the summit account above. Leaders were expected to adopt a Shenzhen Declaration before the meeting closed, with Moscow’s support for the draft text confirmed by President Putin, in the pledge account.

The two bilaterals followed, and each produced one sentence that carries the day. At the bilateral meeting with President Xi, held at the Kylin Villa, the President said the two share a strong consensus that oil transport through the Strait of Hormuz should take place, and asked President Xi to do more for American farmers, in the summit account above, which grades the sentence as the President’s, reported by Reuters and carried by Yonhap, on a single wire chain, with no Chinese or American official reaction quoted in that report; the President also called President Xi his friend and said the two leaders have a very special relationship, in the same account. Earlier, the President and President Putin met one on one in Shenzhen, in the same account’s live coverage: the President told President Putin that a lot of wonderful things could come out of the meeting and, in a separate White House video, pointed at him and called him his friend. Against the meeting stands the wire’s reading of the photograph: the two men shared a brief handshake and a few words at a photo opportunity, Russia’s Interfax agency said they did not have a substantive conversation there, and Russian officials said no full-scale bilateral negotiations were planned at the one-on-one, in the wire account filed below. Before the meetings, the President told Fox News he would welcome an agreement with China and Russia to cut nuclear arsenals, put the American stockpile at about 4,000 warheads against 3,800 for Russia and 400 to 500 for China, and said he would accept inspections in all three countries, in the summit account.

The three-way room itself had not reported by the night’s last bearing. The formal trilateral session stood scheduled for later on Thursday and no agreement or joint statement had been reported by midday in Shenzhen, in the summit account; the Kremlin aide Mr. Ushakov said on Monday that the three countries were in intensive consultations over a draft joint statement and that Russia had conveyed its position to China, and it remained unclear whether a statement would be adopted, in the Yonhap account filed below. The expectations printed ahead of the session stand unamended: no major agreements expected, in the wire account and in the Yalta account filed below, which records that no agenda has been published and no joint statement announced. On Ukraine, the signals conflict in the open: Washington had signalled the war was not expected to be addressed in the three-way meeting before the President said it would, in the summit account, and White House officials have said he is not expected to raise it there, in the wire account. The reactions from outside the room stand in the summit account: Ukraine’s foreign minister, Mr. Sybiga, said in Kyiv he hoped Presidents Xi and Trump would put “pressure on Russia to end the war,” and Canada’s Prime Minister, Mr. Carney, in Shenzhen for the summit, said sanctions on Russia would “continue to increase as long as this war goes on.” On the fourth chair, no meeting with Mr. Kim is planned on this trip in American officials’ repeated words, in the wire account. After the trilateral, the President is scheduled to depart Shenzhen for Washington, in the same account. Settled: the plenary, the pledge, and both bilaterals. Open: the room, and what, if anything, it signs.

Asia at 0400: Taiwan Down 4.4 Percent at the Close and 7.22 on the Smaller Board, Tokyo and Seoul Higher, Hong Kong Down Two, and Australia’s Jobless Rate at 4.9

Asia’s Thursday session split on the same line as Wednesday’s: the chip markets that host the trade fell or rose with it, and Taiwan fell hardest. Taiwan’s benchmark ended down 4.4 percent, in the wire account above, at 38,426.89 in the exchange account filed below, which carries the island’s smaller-company index, the TPEx, down 7.22 percent at 285.33, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing down 3.45 percent and MediaTek down 5.58 percent in the reports it cites. The session’s path ran through a fall of 3.73 percent at 0351 GMT in the early account filed below and a drop of as much as 4.8 percent in the slide account filed below; the closing figures printed elsewhere stand apart from the wire’s and are carried in the Cocked Hat. Japan’s Nikkei 225 rose 0.70 percent to the 59,450 level and South Korea’s Kospi rose 0.55 percent to about 5,095.30, while Hong Kong’s Hang Seng fell 2.19 percent to about 22,790 and the Shanghai Composite fell 0.69 percent to 3,563.56, in the divergence account filed below; a second account of the chip markets puts the Nikkei up about 1 percent over 59,334, with SoftBank Group and Tokyo Electron each up about 3 percent, the Kospi up 0.79 percent at 5,079.54, SK Hynix up 4.19 percent and Samsung Electronics up 2.31 percent, and the Hang Seng down 1.12 percent at 22,816.43 with its technology index down 2.5 percent to a four-month low, in the rally account filed below. The two readings are successive and rival at once, and both stand.

Taiwan’s answer came from its regulator the same day. The Financial Supervisory Commission said on Thursday it will enact new short-selling curbs after the benchmark’s fall, in the wire account above: where a stock closes down 3.5 percent or more on a given day, investors may not sell it short the next trading day, through margin short selling or through borrowed securities. The island has already put a $15 billion stock stabilisation fund into operation, alongside previously announced curbs, in the same account; the regulator noted sharp swings in share prices and said stock fundamentals remain fairly solid, listed companies have posted record revenue, and the capital market is resilient, in the same account. The wire’s sentence for the cause stands as its sentence: investors unnerved by the future of artificial intelligence after Mr. Huang resigned as Nvidia’s chief, in the same account.

The day’s two data prints came from Canberra and Tokyo. Australia’s seasonally adjusted unemployment rate jumped to 4.9 percent in October from 4.7 percent, and total employment dropped by 43,500 to a five-month low of 14.74 million, in the divergence account above; the Australian dollar slipped below $0.67 to its lowest level since December, and Australia’s S&P/ASX 200 fell 1.04 percent to 8,730.40, in the same account. Japan’s core machinery orders slipped 0.3 percent on the month in September, against a forecast fall of 0.5 percent, and Governor Ueda told a parliamentary committee that underlying inflation must remain anchored around 2 percent and that the Bank of Japan will continue raising interest rates as economic and price conditions warrant, in the same account; the yen traded around 159.4. Settled: Taiwan’s close, its curbs, and both prints. Open: whether the curbs meet a second falling day on Friday.

New York at 0400: Moody’s Lowers Nvidia’s Outlook to Stable, Futures Stand Higher on the Pricing, and ANT’s First Trade Is Still a Bell Away

The night’s one New York act was a ratings act. Moody’s lowered Nvidia’s credit outlook to stable from positive on Wednesday, citing the departure of Mr. Huang and the absence of a formal succession plan, and affirmed the company’s Aa1 senior unsecured rating and its Prime-1 commercial paper rating, in the ratings account and the agency account filed below. The agency’s senior vice-president, Mr. Joshi, said an upgrade is unlikely over the next 12 to 18 months despite the company’s strong market position and finances, in the agency account, which also carries the agency’s projections—revenue up 96 percent in fiscal 2027 and $746 billion in fiscal 2028—and its figure of $118 billion in guarantees, chiefly connected to a lease guarantee for a data centre campus in Portsmouth, Ohio. The guarantee figure stands against the $164.5 billion of total financial commitments the week’s file carried from the company’s own report, and the two are printed apart in the Cocked Hat. The cost of protecting the company’s debt against default was quoted at 121 basis points late Wednesday, about 20 basis points lower than a week earlier, in the outlook account filed below. The interim chief, Ms. Kress, said on Tuesday the company would maintain a “disciplined” and “rigorous” approach to future investments, in the same account. No word from the board on a permanent successor stands in the overnight file.

Anthropic’s first trade is Thursday’s, and at 0400 it has not happened: the shares are expected to begin trading on the Nasdaq under ANT on Thursday, a large listing usually opening well after the 0930 bell once its opening auction clears, in the debut account and the timing account filed below, the second of which records that when SpaceX listed in June its first trade came at about 11:46 a.m. Eastern. After the offering, Amazon is expected to hold 14.7 percent of the shares outstanding and Google 13.7 percent, in the debut account. The futures that price the day stood higher through the night, in readings that differ by instrument and hour: Nasdaq-100 futures up about 1 percent and S&P 500 futures up about 0.6 percent in the Asia session, in the Asia-Pacific account filed below, and Nasdaq-100 futures up 1.5 percent with S&P 500 futures up 0.9 percent in the futures account filed below, against the night account’s 2113 Eastern readings of up 1.02 and up 0.58 percent in the midnight file. Oil held near $92 for Brent, briefly above $93 in the Asia session in the Asia-Pacific account and at $92.21, up 0.3 percent, in the futures account, with West Texas at $83.17; gold stood near $3,730, down about 0.4 percent, in the Asia-Pacific account and at about $3,720 in the morning brief filed below, which puts the dollar index near 103.9, its highest in 19 months. Settled: the outlook, and the night’s direction. Open: the first trade, which will set the market price the $83 offering price only proposes.

The Gulf at 0400: Three More Tankers Claimed on Mines East of the Strait, None Named, and No Word on the Radar for a Sixth Day

The strait’s arithmetic grew again on Wednesday evening, on a claim. Iran’s army said three violating tankers caught fire and ground to a halt after striking naval mines in the eastern Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday, after entering an unauthorized maritime area despite repeated warnings, with their navigation systems switched off, in the army’s account above; a companion account attributes the same evening claim to the Guards, relayed through the state broadcaster, and carries the sentence that passage through the waterway must be coordinated with Iranian authorities, in the claim account filed below. The claim arrived with no vessel name, flag, owner or cargo, no casualty figure and no position more precise than east of the strait, and Reuters could not independently confirm it, in the claim audit filed below, which sets the week’s claims in a table against what has been confirmed and records that the evening claim may be one announcement reported two ways, by the Guards and by the regular army, the two naval forces Tehran fields. The wire’s agency version stands in the agency account filed below: three more oil tankers struck mines and caught fire, the ships unable to manoeuvre, the claims not independently verified at this stage. The desk prints the claim as a claim, at its full size and with its full absence of names.

The named ship in the strait gained no ending in the night. Searches continued on Wednesday to locate the missing seafarer from the Tara Gas and officials in Oman were still trying to put out the fire aboard her, in the wire account filed below; the night’s fullest restatement of the ship’s file, published at 0003 UTC on Thursday, carries the same position—24 of 25 crew rescued, 21 Indian seafarers ashore at Khasab, two in hospital, one still missing, the fire’s footage widely shared and not independently verified—in the restatement account filed below. The injury counts stand apart as they have stood: eleven injured in the operator’s statement, two in hospital in the authorities’, unblended. On the mechanism that struck the ships, the file’s split stands where the week left it: mines in Tehran’s accounts, an unknown projectile in the maritime centre’s report of the Tuesday strike, in the claim audit above.

Bahrain and Kuwait took Wednesday’s round, and the radar question took another day of silence. Bahrain’s defence force reported it had intercepted another round of Iranian aerial attacks on Wednesday and its interior ministry issued two more threat alerts—the fourth attack wave on Bahrain in six days—and Iran’s regular army said on Wednesday its drones had targeted Patriot systems and launchers at the Ali al-Salem base in Kuwait, with no casualties or damage confirmed in the initial reporting, in the Bahrain account filed below. Qatar’s foreign ministry condemned the renewed attacks on Bahrain and Kuwait in its November 18 statement as violations of their sovereignty, in the condemnation account filed below, which also carries Bahrain’s call for full implementation of Security Council Resolution 2817. On the radar the Guards said they destroyed on November 13, no assessment of the machine itself—hit, missed or intact—stands from any capital in the overnight file, for a sixth day; the intercepts are reported, the machine is not, and the desk records the silence as a silence. Settled: Wednesday’s intercepts, and the condemnation. Open: the fire, the missing man, the three claimed tankers, and the radar.

France and Spain at 0400: The Retirees March Today and the Senate Takes the Police Bill, and Spain’s Debate Stands at 2200 With Its Instruments Still Apart

France’s Thursday is a marching and a debating day, and both were set before the night began. Retirees plan to march in Paris on Thursday, union representatives were due to meet the Prime Minister, Mr. Lecornu, and on Thursday he holds talks with political parties about the protests, in the day-ahead account filed below, which also carries Tuesday’s strike at 146,000 in the official count against more than 500,000 in the unions’, and the coordinated cost-of-living demonstrations called in seven European countries for November 20, 21 and 22. The contested police bill, which would give officers a presumption of legitimate self-defence when they use firearms, has passed the lower house and heads to the Senate, in the same account; the Senate debates it on Thursday, with a protest outside the Senate in the day’s Paris schedule as the evening file carried it. The bill’s passage in the National Assembly in July and its Senate examination today stand in the week’s accounts, in the turnout account filed below. Settled: the day’s order. Open: the march’s size, and the Senate’s vote.

Spain’s Thursday is one room, at 2200. The head-to-head debate between Mr. Sánchez and Mr. Feijóo is organised by the Television Academy at the Madrid Content City studio in Tres Cantos, moderated by its president, Ms. Casado, on five topics—housing; the economy and taxes; social policy and public services; fighting corruption; and migration and foreign policy—in the debate account filed below. The instruments the debate must move stand where Wednesday left them, apart. The daily tracking’s sixth instalment puts the Popular Party at 32.2 percent and the Socialists at 30.7, a gap of 1.5 points, with Vox at 17.0 percent, down half a point on the day and 1.8 points since the tracking began, and the Socialists’ seats up two to 122, in the polls account filed below; the same instalment’s seat table stands at 131 for the Popular Party in the tracking account filed below and at 133 in the table of the average account filed below, which puts the survey of surveys at 128 seats for the Popular Party, 111 for the Socialists and 65 for Vox, on vote estimates of 30.8, 27.5 and 19.1 percent across 19 institutes. Mr. Sánchez remains the preferred candidate to lead the government, at 32.4 percent in the tracking’s reading in the polls account and 32.8 in its earlier instalment, against Mr. Feijóo at 22.5 and 22.2 in the same two readings. Polls may publish until November 23; Spain votes November 29. Settled: the hour, the room and the topics. Open: which instrument Spain believes after tonight.

Thursday Opens: A Report at 0600 Central, Claims at 0830, a First Trade, a Declaration, and a Debate at 2200

Thursday carries Walmart’s third-quarter release at 6 a.m. Central with its call at 7 a.m. Central, in the company’s notice filed below, against consensus of $0.64 a share on revenue of $187.24 billion and the company’s own guide of $0.62 to $0.64, in the calendar account filed below; weekly jobless claims and the Philadelphia Fed survey at 0830 Eastern, against forecasts of 197,000 to 198,000 in the night account the midnight file carried; the first trade of ANT on the Nasdaq, at no scheduled hour; the Shenzhen Declaration’s adoption and the trilateral’s readout in Shenzhen, after which the President departs for Washington; the retirees’ march and the police bill in Paris; and Spain’s debate at 2200. Japan’s national consumer prices for October are due Friday at 2330 GMT, in the Asia-Pacific account above. The Senate Commerce Committee is owed its technical answers on the ground stop by November 23, the last day Spanish polls may publish. Alaska certifies on November 25, the day the Treasury Secretary’s ten days also run to. Spain votes November 29; the Federal Reserve decides December 8 and 9; government funding runs out after December 11. The Midday Watch collects at 1200.

The Cocked Hat

Where the night’s bearings do not meet, the desk prints the triangle. On the villa: Kylin Villa in the summit trade’s spelling and Qilin Villa in the summit account’s. On the Putin meeting: a one-on-one held, with wonderful things promised, in the live coverage; no substantive conversation at the photo opportunity and no full-scale negotiations planned, in the wire’s and the Russian officials’ readings. On the Hormuz sentence: a strong consensus, spoken by one president, carried on one wire chain, with no reaction from the other capital quoted. On the statement: intensive consultations over a draft in the Kremlin aide’s account, adoption unclear in the wire’s, and no agreement expected in the officials’ and analysts’ readings. On Taiwan’s close: down 4.4 percent in the wire and in the exchange account’s 38,426.89, down 4.57 percent at 38,359 in one market table, down 4.60 percent at 38,348 in one morning pulse, and down 3.24 percent at 38,891.68 in one recap—with the smaller board’s 7.22 percent a different index, not a bigger fall of the same one. On Asia’s closes: the Nikkei up 0.70 percent in one account and about 1 percent in another, the Kospi up 0.55 and up 0.79 in the same two, and the Hang Seng down 2.19, down 2.11 and down 1.12 across three readings of the session. On Nvidia’s guarantees: $118 billion in the ratings agency’s figure, chiefly one campus lease, against $164.5 billion of total commitments in the company file the week carried. On the strait’s evening claim: three tankers in the army’s account and in the agency’s, the same claim attributed to the Guards in a second chain, one announcement possibly reported two ways, and no name, flag or confirmation from any party not making the claim. On futures: Nasdaq-100 up 1.02 percent at 2113 Eastern, about 1 percent in the Asia session and 1.5 percent in one futures account. On Spain: the Popular Party at 131 seats in one printing of the sixth tracking and 133 in another’s table, Vox at 55 in the tracking and 71 in Sondaxe, and the Socialists first in the state pollster’s instrument and second in every other. On Walmart’s consensus: $0.64 a share in every account, on ranges of $0.61 to $0.66 and $0.62 to $0.66, and revenue expected at $187.24 billion, $187.25 billion and $186.5 billion in three readings. Inside the triangle is where the week honestly stands, and the log turns on it.

The Clippings Filed With This Edition

Everything the desk read for the report above, clipped and filed as a bureau files it. Each item is stamped subjective—a source with a position, printed because it is useful—and described by what it says. The desk’s report is the only item in this edition stamped objective. 43 items.

Subjective
Kilambi News — Xi, Trump and Putin Gather in Shenzhen for First Trilateral Summit

The account, updated through the morning of November 19, carries the Trump-Xi bilateral at the villa in Shenzhen, at which the President said the two share a strong consensus that oil transport through the Strait of Hormuz should take place and asked President Xi to do more for American farmers; the Trump-Putin one-on-one held earlier in Shenzhen; the President’s Fox News remarks welcoming an agreement to cut nuclear arsenals, with stockpile figures and inspections; President Xi’s opening of the APEC leaders’ meeting, with lower barriers and $20 million for regional cooperation; and the formal trilateral still scheduled for later on Thursday, with no agreement or joint statement reported by midday in Shenzhen. The account grades its own chains: the Hormuz and farm remarks are the President’s as reported by Reuters and carried by Yonhap, and no Chinese or American official reaction is quoted.

Subjective
Reuters, carried by BusinessWorld — Trump’s Historic Meeting With Xi, Putin Headlines Asia Trip

The wire account carries Thursday’s order in Shenzhen: a bilateral meeting and working lunch with President Xi ahead of the trilateral, a one-on-one with President Putin at which Russian officials said no full-scale bilateral negotiations were planned, and the trilateral itself, bringing together the leaders of the three largest nuclear powers, with the President pressing nuclear arms control against Beijing’s resistance to making it a centrepiece. It carries the brief handshake at the photo opportunity, with Interfax reporting no substantive conversation there; White House officials saying the President is not expected to raise the war in Ukraine during the trilateral; the trade truce’s durability as a subject of the bilateral; and the President’s departure for Washington after the trilateral, concluding a trip through the Philippines and China.

Subjective
Yonhap — Trump, Xi, Putin Set to Hold Historic Trilateral Summit; U.S.-North Korea Meeting Uncertain

The account carries the three leaders set to hold their first-ever trilateral summit in Shenzhen on Thursday, on the sidelines of the APEC summit, to discuss international security issues, with uncertainty over a meeting with Mr. Kim; the President’s stated intention to discuss nuclear arms reductions; the Kremlin aide Mr. Ushakov’s statement that the three countries were in intensive consultations over a draft joint statement, with Russia’s position conveyed to China, and that it remains unclear whether a statement will be adopted; and photographs of the welcome reception and of the President’s arrival for the bilateral at the villa, noting that a bilateral meeting with President Putin and a separate bilateral with President Xi were both held ahead of the three-way meeting.

Subjective
Magna Bureau — Xi, Trump and Putin Meet in Shenzhen, and the World Reaches for the Word Yalta

The account carries the first three-way meeting of the three presidents on Thursday in Shenzhen, at the Kylin Villa, on the sidelines of the APEC summit, with nuclear arms, Ukraine and the war with Iran on the table and no agreement expected; the White House’s confirmation of the meeting on November 13 and Beijing’s on November 16; the expiry of New START in February; the sequence of the day, plenary at 09:45, then the bilateral and working lunch, then the three-way session; the trade truce extended on November 9 and running to January 10; and the statement that no agenda has been published and no joint statement announced, with the reporting reviewed not settling whether symbolism or substance will dominate.

Subjective
AsiaToday — Xi Pledges $20 Million for APEC Cooperation as Shenzhen Summit Closes

The account carries President Xi’s pledge of $20 million to support practical cooperation among APEC economies on Thursday, at the closing day of the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders’ Meeting in Shenzhen, with a programme of four pillars—economy and trade, connectivity, innovation and development—and the leaders expected to adopt the Shenzhen Declaration before the meeting closed, with President Putin having confirmed Moscow’s support for the draft text, and the day set to end with the first trilateral meeting alongside a separate Trump-Putin bilateral.

Subjective
KhabarWire — APEC Opens as Trump, Xi and Putin Meet in Shenzhen

The account carries the opening of the APEC leaders’ plenary in Shenzhen on November 19, beginning just before 10:00 local time with a group photograph, President Xi’s $20 million pledge, and the three-way meeting due later that day and not yet begun when the account was published, its agenda, duration and any joint statement unknown; the expected bilateral between the Presidents as their third meeting of the year; the one-on-one with President Putin confirmed by an American official; the trade truce due to expire on January 10, 2027; and the White House’s position that it does not expect a formal agreement.

Subjective
India Strategic — All Eyes on Shenzhen as Trump, Putin and Xi Meet

The account carries the first formal trilateral meeting of the three leaders in Shenzhen on November 19, on the sidelines of the APEC summit, with no formal agenda announced and the Ukraine conflict and Middle East tensions likely to come up, alongside artificial intelligence governance, technology competition and semiconductor export controls; the one-on-one between the Presidents, their first in-person meeting since August 2025 in Alaska; separate talks between the President and President Xi; and President Putin’s November 18 remark that he expected a “big potential benefit” from the trilateral meeting, made at the opening of the APEC CEO summit in Shenzhen.

Subjective
Reuters — Taiwan to Enact New Short-Selling Curbs in Response to Market Drop

The wire account carries the Financial Supervisory Commission’s statement on Thursday that it will enact new short-selling curbs after the benchmark index ended down 4.4 percent, with investors unnerved by the future of artificial intelligence after Mr. Huang resigned as Nvidia’s chief; the new restriction, that a stock closing down 3.5 percent or more may not be sold short the next trading day through margin short selling or borrowed securities; the $15 billion stock stabilisation fund already in operation and the previously announced curbs; and the regulator’s statement that share prices have swung sharply while stock fundamentals remain fairly solid, listed companies have posted record revenue, and the capital market is resilient.

Subjective
Forbis, on the exchange data — Taiwan TPEx Index Drops 7.2 Percent as Smaller Stocks Slide

The account carries the Taipei Exchange’s daily index data for November 19: the TPEx index fell 7.22 percent to 285.33, down 22.22 points from Wednesday’s 307.55, while the larger exchange’s weighted benchmark closed down 4.40 percent at 38,426.89 in the closing report it cites; a mid-morning reading of the TPEx down more than 7 percent with the benchmark down 4.05 percent; selling across semiconductor, server, cooling and circuit-board shares; Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing finishing down 3.45 percent and MediaTek down 5.58 percent in the reports cited; and the session coming ahead of Anthropic’s planned American trading debut.

Subjective
Finimize — Taiwan Stocks Slid as Asia Repriced the AI Trade

The account carries Taipei’s benchmark down almost 5 percent on Thursday, down as much as 4.8 percent in the session and more than 10 percent for the week, dragging regional markets lower as investors trimmed Asia’s artificial intelligence and chip positions ahead of the meeting of the three presidents and fresh scrutiny of American chip export rules; the exchange saying it is ready to curb “irrational” selling if volatility looks abnormal; and the reading that Taiwan’s index, concentrated in a handful of giant chip-linked companies, trades as the region’s high-beta proxy for the artificial intelligence trade.

Subjective
Finimize — Taiwan Tightens Short Selling After a 4.4 Percent Stock Slide

The account carries the regulator’s tightening of short-selling rules after the benchmark slid 4.4 percent, as investors reassessed the outlook for artificial intelligence shares: a stock that closes down 3.5 percent or more may not be shorted the next day, whether through margin shorting or borrowing shares to sell; the island’s central place in the advanced semiconductor supply chain; and the regulators’ position that company fundamentals still look solid, stated alongside the block.

Subjective
Seeking Alpha, carried by TradingView — Asian Stocks Diverge on Soft Australian Employment and Anthropic IPO Focus

The account carries Thursday’s mixed Asian session: the Nikkei 225 up 0.70 percent to the 59,450 level with the yen around 159.4; the Kospi up 0.55 percent to about 5,095.30; the Hang Seng down 2.19 percent to about 22,790; the Shanghai Composite down 0.69 percent to 3,563.56 and the Shenzhen Component down 0.67 percent; the ASX 200 down 1.04 percent to 8,730.40 with the Australian dollar below $0.67 at its lowest since December; Australia’s October unemployment rate at 4.9 percent, up from 4.7, with employment down 43,500 to 14.74 million; Japan’s core machinery orders down 0.3 percent on the month in September against a 0.5 percent fall forecast; Governor Ueda’s statement that the Bank of Japan will continue raising rates as conditions warrant; gold around $3,700 and crude around $83; and Bitcoin sliding toward $62,000 on Wednesday to its lowest since mid-July.

Subjective
Coinpedia — Asian Markets Split After Nvidia Rally: Nikkei and KOSPI Rise, Hang Seng Falls

The account carries the Nikkei up around 1 percent to trade over 59,334.28 after Nvidia’s third-quarter revenue of $115.8 billion, with SoftBank Group and Tokyo Electron each up around 3 percent and Trend Micro up 6 percent; the Kospi up around 0.79 percent to 5,079.54, with SK Hynix up 4.19 percent and Samsung Electronics up 2.31 percent; the Hang Seng down 1.12 percent to 22,816.43 with its technology index down 2.5 percent to a four-month low, Alibaba down 2.63 percent, Tencent down 6.5 percent, Baidu down 2.7 percent and MiniMax down around 10 percent; the pressure from expanded American restrictions on advanced chip exports and remote computing access; and the President’s statement to APEC leaders that the United States opposes “any form of robust regulation” that could control or limit the development of superintelligence.

Subjective
The Edge — Asia Market Wrap, November 19: Early Session, Taiex Drops 3.73 Percent as Most Indices Fall

The account carries Thursday’s early session at 03:51 GMT, with seven of nine indices in the red: Taiwan’s Taiex leading the declines at 38,697.09, down 3.73 percent, and the Nikkei 225 up 0.21 percent; Asian stocks sliding as fears over the artificial intelligence trade and hawkish comments from Federal Reserve officials kept sentiment fragile ahead of Anthropic’s market debut, on the wire reporting it cites; and the note that the sources read gave no reason specific to Taiwan’s fall. The readings are intraday snapshots, not closes, measured against the prior session’s closes.

Subjective
NordFX — Market Pulse, November 19, 2026: Fed Hike Bets Hit Markets

The account carries its Thursday scoreboard: the VIX at 24.6; Nvidia faded after its earnings and Moody’s cut its outlook after Mr. Huang’s exit; the Nikkei up 0.46 percent at 59,298, the Hang Seng down 2.11 percent at 22,803, Shanghai down 0.52 percent at 3,569, the Kospi flat at 5,068, Taiwan down 4.60 percent at 38,348 and the Nifty 50 up 0.33 percent at 25,312; and the day’s calendar of American jobless claims and the Philadelphia Fed index at 13:30 GMT, Walmart’s earnings, and Anthropic’s Nasdaq debut as ANT, priced at $83.

Subjective
CoinEdition — Asia Market Recap: Taiwan Stocks Slide 3.24 Percent as Chipmakers Retreat

The account carries Asian markets ending Thursday on a mixed note with Taiwan leading the losses: the Taiex down 3.24 percent to 38,891.68, with Largan Precision down a tenth of its value and Foxconn and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing down 3.59 and 2.76 percent; memory makers in Seoul, SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics, along with LG Innotek, trading lower; Anthropic’s pricing at $83, above its $70 to $78 marketing range; and the sector’s weeks of wobbling over whether the technology can earn enough to repay the borrowing behind its data centres and chips.

Subjective
AI Affairs — Moody’s Cuts Nvidia’s Ratings Outlook to Stable After Huang’s Exit

The account carries Moody’s lowering of Nvidia’s outlook to stable from positive on November 18, after the chief’s resignation without a formal succession plan, with the Aa1 senior unsecured rating and the Prime-1 commercial paper rating affirmed and an upgrade unlikely over the next 12 to 18 months; the senior vice-president Mr. Joshi’s statement to that effect; the agency’s projections of revenue up 96 percent in fiscal 2027 and $746 billion in fiscal 2028; and its identification of $118 billion in guarantees, chiefly a residual value guarantee linked to OpenAI’s lease payments for a data centre campus in Portsmouth, Ohio.

Subjective
Dow Jones, carried by TradingView — Moody’s Lowers Nvidia Rating Outlook Following Huang Departure

The account carries Moody’s lowering of its ratings outlook for Nvidia to stable from positive on Wednesday, the sudden departure of a key executive without a formal succession plan as the main driver, the affirmation of the Aa1 senior unsecured rating and the Prime-1 short-term commercial paper rating, and Mr. Joshi’s statement that an upgrade is unlikely in the next 12 to 18 months even though the company’s financial position remains exceptionally strong, with the departure having introduced uncertainty about business strategy and financial policies.

Subjective
Business Today — Moody’s Cuts Nvidia’s Credit Outlook to Stable Following Jensen Huang’s Exit

The account carries the outlook cut to stable from positive, the Aa1 rating as the second-highest investment-grade grade and unlikely to be upgraded over the next 12 to 18 months, analyst Mr. Joshi’s statement that the exit introduced uncertainty around strategy and financial policies while market leadership and financial position remained exceptionally strong, the five-year credit default swaps quoted at 121 basis points late Wednesday, about 20 basis points lower than a week earlier, and the interim chief Ms. Kress’s Tuesday statement that the company would maintain a “disciplined” and “rigorous” approach to future investments across the artificial intelligence supply chain.

Subjective
Moneyta — Anthropic IPO Day: What ANT Would Do to Your Portfolio

The account carries the pricing at $83 on November 18, above the $70 to $78 range, the offering enlarged to about 980 million shares with up to 20 percent expected for individual investors, a further filing registering 155 million more shares, the underwriters represented by Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley, and the first trade expected on November 19; the statement that only investors who receive an allocation pay the offering price and that a large new listing usually opens well after the 0930 bell once the Nasdaq opening auction clears; Amazon expected to hold 14.7 percent after the offering and Google 13.7 percent; holders of about 15.5 billion shares under lock-up limits, with up to 315 million shares saleable from the first trading day; and the offering facts as drawn from the registration filings of November 17 and 18.

Subjective
Cold Book Fly — When Can I Buy Anthropic Stock? What Time ANT Starts Trading Around the World

The account carries the first trading day as Thursday, November 19, 2026, with the first trade coming only after Nasdaq’s opening cross, which for large offerings is usually later than the 0930 Eastern bell; the precedent that when SpaceX listed in June its first trade came at about 11:46 a.m. Eastern; the pricing at $83.00 on November 18, above the $70 to $78 range marketed, with the registration declared effective the same day and the offering expected to close November 20; and the sequence of the listing from the October 26 filing naming the Nasdaq Global Select Market and the ticker ANT.

Subjective
investingLive — Asia-Pacific Market News: Oil Holds Near $92 as Gulf Attacks Mount

The account carries Thursday’s Asia session: Anthropic’s confirmed pricing at $83 on 980 million shares in an $81 billion deal and its debut as ANT later Thursday; Brent briefly above $93 before settling around $92 and West Texas near $82, with traders weighing fresh signs of escalation across the Gulf; gold futures down about 0.4 percent near $3,730 after a brief dip below $3,700; Bitcoin down about 1 percent to around $63,700; American equity futures firmer, with Nasdaq-100 futures up about 1 percent and S&P 500 futures up around 0.6 percent; and the day’s calendar of jobless claims and the Philadelphia Fed survey at 0830 Eastern, Walmart before the open, Anthropic’s debut, and Japan’s national consumer prices due at 2330 GMT on Friday.

Subjective
Medium — Anthropic IPO Lifts US Futures as Jobs Weigh on Aussie

The account carries the pricing at $83, above the $70 to $78 range, in an upsized offering and private placement together put at $107.3 billion and described as the biggest listing on record; Nasdaq-100 futures up 1.5 percent and S&P 500 futures up 0.9 percent after the S&P 500’s fifth straight decline; the shares due to trade Thursday as ANT at a fully diluted valuation of about $1.5 trillion; Brent up 0.3 percent to $92.21 and West Texas down 0.1 percent to $83.17 after Wednesday’s 3.2 percent drop on the larger-than-expected rise in crude stocks; gold up 0.2 percent to $3,731 after a 3.2 percent slide to its lowest in more than a year; Euro Stoxx 50 futures up 0.4 percent; and the day’s roadmap of claims, the Philadelphia Fed survey, Vice Chair Jefferson’s speech, the Kansas City Fed survey, the debut, and Japan’s consumer prices.

Subjective
Samuel and Co Trading — Anthropic’s Record Launch: Morning Brief, November 19

The account carries the pricing at $83 above the range and American futures higher, Nasdaq-100 contracts up close to 1 percent and S&P 500 futures up about 0.6 percent in early London trade; Wednesday’s close at 7,323.63 for the S&P 500, the Dow down 561 points to 50,198.17 and the Nasdaq Composite at 24,429.88, with energy shares the worst performers, down about 3.5 percent; oil near its lowest in almost three months, Brent around $92 and American crude near $83, with Iraq’s restart of flows through the Kirkuk-to-Ceyhan pipeline after a 12-year halt given as the supply reason; gold around $3,720; the dollar index near 103.9, its highest in 19 months; the 10-year Treasury yield just above 5.05 percent and the 2-year near 4.79 percent; a fair value of $92 put on Anthropic by Morningstar; Walmart reporting before the open as the read on the American consumer; and Anthropic’s first trade, likely in the American afternoon, as the headline.

Subjective
Press TV — Iran’s Army: Three Violating Tankers Catch Fire After Striking Naval Mines in Strait of Hormuz

The account carries the Army’s statement of Wednesday: three violating tankers caught fire and ground to a halt after striking naval mines in the eastern Strait of Hormuz, after entering an unauthorized maritime area in violation of regulations and despite repeated warnings from the Iranian Navy, the vessels having operated in the area since earlier in the day with their navigation systems switched off; the announcement following a separate Guards statement that a third oil tanker had exploded on Tuesday after navigating a similarly unauthorized route; and the force’s description of the number of vessels striking mines in the area over the preceding two weeks as “unprecedented.”

Subjective
House of Saud — Iran Claims 3 Tankers Hit Mines East of Hormuz

The account carries the evening claim of November 18—three oil tankers caught fire after hitting naval mines east of the strait—attributed through one chain to the Guards and through another to Tehran’s army, with the morning’s confirmed incident of the ADNOC vessel, one crew member missing and 11 injured, set against it; the absence of any vessel name, flag, owner or cargo, any casualty figure, or any position more precise than east of the strait, and the wire’s inability to confirm the incident; the line carried in the Guards’ statement that passage through the waterway must be coordinated with Iranian authorities; the note that Iran fields two separate naval forces, both issuing statements about Hormuz in the past week, so the evening claim may be one announcement reported two ways; and a table setting the past week’s Iranian claims against what has been independently confirmed.

Subjective
DPA, carried by Ekkow — Iran Reports Explosions on Three Tankers Near Strait of Hormuz

The agency account carries Iran’s Navy reporting explosions on ships east of the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday, on the state media’s reporting: three more oil tankers struck mines and caught fire, the crews having ignored warnings while sailing in restricted zones with their navigation systems switched off, and the ships unable to manoeuvre; the Guards’ claim of control of the strait and its view of transits as a violation of an agreement with the United States; and the statement that the claims could not be independently verified at this stage.

Subjective
ZeroHedge — IRGC Says 3 More Tankers on Fire After Ignoring Warnings in Hormuz Area

The account carries the Wednesday update that the Guards claimed three more attacks on oil tankers which caught fire, the three said to have hit mines east of the strait after ignoring warnings while navigating restricted areas with navigation systems disabled, and the statement carried by the state broadcaster that passage through the waterway must be coordinated with Iranian authorities; the Tara Gas file in the same account, abandoned on Tuesday after a second hit, one Indian sailor still missing, 24 crew evacuated by Oman’s authorities about two nautical miles off the Musandam coast, 21 brought ashore at Khasab and two in hospital in India’s count; and the ship among five tankers reported hit around Hormuz on Tuesday.

Subjective
Reuters, carried by KTWB — UAE’s ADNOC L&S Says One Crew Member Missing After Attack on Its Vessel in Hormuz

The wire account carries the operator’s Wednesday statement that one crew member was missing and 11 injured after one of its vessels was attacked in the strait on Tuesday, the rest of the crew evacuated and the vessel not named; Oman’s authorities having rescued 24 crew members from the Panama-flagged Tara Gas, with the search continuing for one missing person and efforts to put out the fire aboard the tanker still under way; the maritime sources’ account that the Tara Gas crew abandoned ship on Tuesday after the vessel was struck by a projectile; the ship’s ownership and management listings; Tehran’s Tuesday statement that a ship carrying liquefied gas and two oil tankers had caught fire in the waterway; and the British agency’s report that the crew of a tanker was unaccounted for after a second attack north of Khasab.

Subjective
National Security Journal — India Just Got Pulled Into the Hormuz Crisis: 24 of Its Sailors Were on a Gas Tanker Struck Twice

The account, published at 0003 UTC on November 19, carries the Tara Gas struck twice on Monday and Tuesday in the strait, one person still missing, two hospitalized, and footage of smoke and flames widely shared and not independently verified; the first attack reported by the British maritime centre around 1900 UTC on Monday, about seven nautical miles north of Khasab; the second strike on Tuesday forcing the crew to abandon ship; 24 crew rescued by Oman’s navy and coast guard, 21 Indian crew members taken ashore at Khasab, two Indian nationals in hospital and one remaining missing in India’s foreign ministry count; searches continuing on Wednesday and Omani officials still trying to put out the fire, on the wire’s reporting; the operator’s separate Wednesday statement of one missing and 11 injured aboard one of its vessels attacked on Tuesday evening; and the maritime organisation’s figure of 138 incidents and 25 confirmed crew deaths as of November 17.

Subjective
Splash 247 — Hormuz Inferno Leaves Seafarer Missing

The account carries an Indian seafarer missing and two others injured after the liquefied petroleum gas carrier Tara Gas was struck twice in the strait, the Panama-flagged, 53,200-tonne vessel abandoned after the second strike on Tuesday engulfed it in flames off Oman’s Musandam Peninsula; India’s foreign ministry confirming 24 of the 25 crew rescued, including 21 Indian nationals brought ashore at Khasab, two injured Indian sailors in hospital, and a search continuing for the missing seafarer; and the British maritime centre’s first report of the attack on Monday, seven nautical miles north of Khasab.

Subjective
House of Saud — Bahrain Demands UN Guarantees as Iran Drones Hit Kuwait

The account carries the campaign of the past six days: the Guards’ attacks on American installations in Bahrain four times over six days, Bahrain’s case taken to the Security Council with a demand for guarantees, and on Wednesday the regular army’s widening of the campaign to an American airbase in Kuwait, its statement that its drones targeted Patriot systems and launchers at the Ali al-Salem base, with no casualties or damage confirmed in the initial reporting; Wednesday’s further round intercepted by Bahrain’s defence force with two more interior ministry alerts; the three Bahrain facilities targeted across the waves—the early-warning radar of November 13, the Al-Riffa air-defence radar of November 15 and the Sheikh Isa radar of November 17; and Gulf states presenting evidence of more than 7,000 Iranian missiles and drones fired at their territories since the war began on February 28.

Subjective
Dilmun Record — Qatar Condemns Attacks on Bahrain, Extends Rebuke to Kuwait

The account carries Qatar’s foreign ministry statement of November 18 condemning renewed Iranian attacks on Bahrain and Kuwait as flagrant violations of their sovereignty and territorial integrity, with solidarity reaffirmed with both countries; the Guards’ claim of the drone strike it condemned, six drones toward an American air defence radar at Bahrain’s Riffa air base, against Bahrain’s military statement that it intercepted and destroyed all six before they hit their target; Bahrain’s urging of full implementation of Security Council Resolution 2817, which condemned Iranian attacks against Bahrain and other countries in the region and demanded an end to them; and the previous week’s approval by Gulf defence ministers of a new joint command centre in Kuwait.

Subjective
Walmart — Walmart to Host Third Quarter Earnings Conference Call, November 19, 2026

The company’s notice of November 12 carries the release of its third-quarter results at 6 a.m. Central on Thursday, November 19, 2026, with a live conference call with the investment community at 7 a.m. Central, hosted by its president and chief executive, Mr. Furner, and its chief financial officer, Mr. Rainey, and links to the earnings materials.

Subjective
SentiSense — Big Tech Earnings This Week: Nvidia Reports November 17, and Walmart Reports November 19

The account carries the week’s calendar and consensus: Walmart reporting before the open on Thursday, November 19, its fiscal third quarter ended October 31, at a market value of about $1.0 trillion, with consensus of $0.64 a share from 23 analysts on a range of $0.62 to $0.66 and revenue of $187.24 billion from 18 analysts on a range of $186.06 billion to $188.84 billion; the company’s own guide of August 20, for net sales up 3.0 to 3.75 percent and adjusted operating income up 2.0 to 4.0 percent in constant currency and adjusted earnings of $0.62 to $0.64; and the full-year guide of $2.80 to $2.87.

Subjective
Zacks — Walmart’s Q3 Earnings on Deck: Is WMT Stock a Buy or Hold?

The account carries the third-quarter report slated before the market opens on November 19, with the consensus estimate for revenue at $186.5 billion, up 3.9 percent from the year-ago quarter, and for earnings at 64 cents a share, up 3.2 percent, the earnings estimate having risen a penny over the past 30 days; the company’s expectation of net sales growth of 3 to 3.75 percent and operating income growth of 2 to 4 percent in constant currency; and the shares carrying a trailing four-quarter average earnings surprise of 3.9 percent.

Subjective
First Feed News — Market Watch: What Will Move Stocks Thursday

The account carries futures at 2113 Eastern on Wednesday: Dow futures at 50,437, up 164 points or 0.33 percent, S&P 500 futures up 0.58 percent to 7,382.75 and Nasdaq-100 futures up 1.02 percent to 27,463.25 in one quote service’s figures, with a second service’s Nasdaq-100 print at 27,479.25, up 1.08 percent; Wednesday’s close in its figures; Palo Alto Networks at $370.78 after hours, up another 9.08 percent, and Nvidia at $151.94, up 0.65 percent; Asia’s early Thursday readings; and Thursday’s calendar, with Walmart before the open and jobless claims and the Philadelphia Fed survey at 0830.

Subjective
Trending Keywords — Trending Searches in France Today: Strike Turnout Falls as Retirees Prepare to March

The account carries France’s nationwide pay strike drawn far fewer people than the last big mobilisation, at 146,000 in the official count against the unions’ claim of more than 500,000; union representatives due to meet the Prime Minister and, on Thursday, his talks with political parties about the protests, ahead of presidential elections due in April and May next year; retirees planning to march in Paris on Thursday; trade unions and housing organisations in seven European countries calling coordinated cost-of-living demonstrations on November 20, 21 and 22; and the contested police bill, giving officers a presumption of legitimate self-defence when they use firearms, passed by the lower house and heading to the Senate.

Subjective
Unbiased Headlines — France Holds Fifth Straight Saturday of Protests as Turnout Falls to 106,000

The account carries the fifth consecutive Saturday of nationwide protests on November 14, the Interior Ministry’s count at about 106,000 nationwide, including 24,000 in Paris, the lowest turnout in recent weeks, against organisers’ 200,000; the movement’s grievances across students, education unions, Yellow Vest activists and child-protection campaigners; the government’s promised 0.6 percent minimum wage increase, rejected by the unions with another strike day called for Tuesday; and the police bill giving officers a presumption of legitimate self-defence when they use their weapons, approved by the lower house and due to go before the Senate, with its supporters’ argument that officers should not automatically be suspected of using disproportionate force.

Subjective
Costa — Election 29N: Campaign Under Way, Sánchez-Feijóo Debate on 19th

The account carries the official campaign for the November 29 general election, begun on Friday, November 13; the head-to-head debate between Mr. Sánchez and Mr. Feijóo on Thursday, November 19, organised by the Television Academy and moderated by its president, Ms. Casado, at the Madrid Content City studio in Tres Cantos, on five topics—housing; the economy and taxes; social policy and public services; fighting corruption; and migration and foreign policy; the daily tracking after the first day of campaigning, with the gap at 1.3 points and the two right parties together at about 190 seats against the 176 needed, their combined vote share dipping just below 50 percent for the first time since May; the state pollster having the Socialists in first place the day before; and polls publishable until Monday, November 23.

Subjective
The Geneva Times — Who Do Polls Say Will Win the Spanish Election?

The account carries the polls with eleven days to the November 29 vote: the daily tracking’s sixth instalment, with Vox at 17 percent, down half a point on Tuesday, one point on two days and 1.8 points since the tracking began, the Popular Party gaining four-tenths on the day and seven-tenths in two days to 32.2 percent, the Socialists up one-tenth to 30.7 percent, the gap at 1.5 points, and the Socialists’ seats up two to 122, with a range of 118 to 127; the right bloc’s range across polls of 179 seats at worst and 199 at best; Mr. Sánchez remaining the preferred candidate to lead the country at 32.4 percent, with Mr. Feijóo rising to 22.5 percent; the poll-of-polls average putting the Popular Party at about 32 percent, the Socialists at 26, Vox at 19 and the left bloc at 7; and the state pollster’s November figure of 33.3 percent for the Socialists, far better than every other pollster’s.

Subjective
Demócrata — General Election Poll: Vox Loses Four Seats and PP and PSOE Advance, According to 40dB Tracking

The account carries the tracking of November 18, placing the Popular Party at 131 seats and the Socialists at 122, with Vox at 55; the presidential preference differences, Mr. Sánchez’s advantage at 10 points over Mr. Feijóo and 16 over Mr. Abascal, with the absolute percentages not provided in that information; the preferred government option remaining a coalition of the Popular Party and Vox, its distance from a Socialist-led executive reduced to one point, nearly four less than at the campaign’s start; and the tracking’s basis of 2,000 online interviews conducted from November 13 to 17, with a margin of error of 2.2 percent.

Subjective
Demócrata — Feijóo Wins the Opinion Poll of the 29N and PP-Vox Maintains a Majority

The account carries the survey of surveys with nine days to the November 29 election: the average placing the Popular Party at 128 seats, the Socialists at 111 and Vox at 65, on vote estimates of 30.8, 27.5 and 19.1 percent across 19 institutes for the vote and 17 for the seats, with the absolute majority at 176; the two daily trackings published Wednesday agreeing on the order, the Popular Party first and the Socialists second, and drawing two very different seat distributions, at 133 seats for the Popular Party and 55 for Vox in one table of the tracking’s figures and 121 and 71 in Sondaxe; the vote estimates behind the difference, Vox at 17 percent in the tracking and 19.4 percent in Sondaxe, and the Socialists at 30.7 percent and 122 seats in the tracking against 27.0 percent and 111 in Sondaxe; and the fieldwork periods and samples of the two instruments.

entry.title: Wednesday Closes With Alaska's House Seat Held by Mr. Begich at 51.35 Percent, Anthropic's Offering Enlarged to 980 Million Shares at $83, Futures Higher at Night, and a Fire Still Burning in the Strait
entry.summary: Wednesday closes with Alaska's House seat held by Mr. Begich at 51.35 percent, Anthropic's offering enlarged to 980 million shares at $83, futures higher at night, and a fire still burning in the strait.
entry.content:
The Midnight File — The Desk’s Report

Objective

Wednesday Closes With Alaska’s House Seat Held by Mr. Begich at 51.35 Percent, Anthropic’s Offering Enlarged to 980 Million Shares at $83, Futures Higher at Night, and a Fire Still Burning in the Strait

The last entry of the day: what the day settled, what it left open, filed before the log turns. A House seat that waited for the tabulation and kept its first-choice leader; a listing whose final size was the evening’s last unknown and is now a number; a market that sold a beat by day and bought the night; an oil settlement that closed the inventory argument for the week; and, in the strait, a fire and a search that no hour on Wednesday closed.

By Eunice, the desk · Collected and analyzed at 0000 ET, Thursday, November 19, 2026. This edition closes the day continued in Edition No. 61, the Evening Watch, collected at 1800 on Wednesday, in Edition No. 60, the Midday Watch, collected at 1200 on Wednesday, and in Edition No. 59, the Morning Watch, collected at 1006 on Wednesday. Those editions stand unrevised, as a log stands. Where the midnight figures differ from the evening figures, the difference is stated here, in the open.

The Midnight in Brief: A Tabulation Held, a Size Set, and a Night That Bought What the Day Sold

Wednesday settled its two waiting counts and its one waiting price, and it left its oldest questions where it found them. Alaska’s Division of Elections ran its tabulation at 2100 Eastern and Mr. Begich held the state’s House seat at 51.35 percent, in the tabulation account filed below. Anthropic’s offering, priced at $83 in the evening file with its final size unstated, stands enlarged to 980 million shares, in the pricing account filed below. Futures at 2113 Eastern stood higher across the board, in the night account filed below. Oil settled lower on the official inventories, in the settlement account filed below. The desk takes the files in that order.

Alaska at Midnight: The Tabulation Ran at 2100 Eastern, Mr. Begich Held at 51.35 Percent, and Three State Races Closed Within Fractions

The count the evening file printed as tonight’s fact ran on time, and it confirmed the models the file had carried for three days. The Division of Elections tabulated 15 contests on Wednesday evening, including the United States House race, four state Senate races and ten state House races, in the tabulation account above. Mr. Begich entered with 47.53 percent of first choices to Mr. Hill’s 41.77, on the Wednesday afternoon report of 290,323 ballots in the afternoon account filed below. After Mr. McDermott’s elimination sent 2,061 ballots to Mr. Begich and 2,012 to Mr. Hill, Mr. Hafner’s elimination sent 10,627 to Mr. Begich and 10,693 to Mr. Hill; Mr. Hill took slightly more of the last transfer and not enough of it, and Mr. Begich finished at 51.35 percent to 48.65, in the tabulation account. The wire’s account of the same tabulation prints the finish at nearly 51.4 percent to nearly 48.7, in the wire account filed below; both printings stand in the Cocked Hat. Mr. Hill called Mr. Begich to congratulate him, in the same account.

The tabulation closed the state’s federal file. The Senate and the governorship were settled on first choices and stand in the tabulation account at 50.13 percent for Ms. Peltola and 51.08 percent for the Kreiss-Tomkins ticket, against the morning file’s Senate count of 144,302 to 131,844; the afternoon account puts Ms. Peltola at 144,486 with her lead at 12,521, and the difference is a day of mail, printed as a difference. Below the federal races, the night’s closest work was in the Mat-Su Valley: one House race turned on three votes after transfers, at 50.02 percent, and two neighbouring races closed at 50.03 and 50.04 percent, all three within the threshold for a state-funded recount if requested, with the five-day request window opening after certification, in the tabulation account. Certification is scheduled for November 25. The court and investigation file outlives the count, as it has since the call: the Justice Department’s appeal, the federal investigation into the second Mr. Sullivan’s recruitment, and Ms. Peltola’s denial of involvement, restated Wednesday in the wire account, stand open. Settled: both of Alaska’s seats in Washington, on the count. Open: certification, any recount requests in the three fractional races, and the cases.

The Fed at Midnight: The Minutes’ Wording Stands, a Measured Voice Joins the Half-Point Voice, and December’s Argument Is Now Only About Size

The minutes published at 1400 stand at midnight as the day’s central document, and the night added one voice to the two the evening file carried. Governor Waller’s half-point position stands in the day’s accounts; Governor Barr’s stands beside it. President Daly, speaking Wednesday, said further hikes will be required and emphasised a measured approach, in the Daly account filed below. The pricing stands apart by instrument: a quarter-point hike fully priced and a hike certain at 100 percent with 94.7 percent on a quarter-point in the pricing account filed below, about 95 percent on a quarter-point in the wire accounts, and 13.6 percent on a half-point in one account’s post-inflation reading, against 5.3 percent in the pricing account’s table. Open: the size, on December 8 and 9, and the data between here and there.
