The Clippings Filed With This Edition

Everything the desk read for the report above, clipped and filed as a bureau files it. Each item is stamped subjective—a source with a position, printed because it is useful—and described by what it says. The desk’s report is the only item in this edition stamped objective. 33 items.

Subjective
Reuters — air travel largely returns to normal on Monday, 300 cancelled by 0900, and the Secretary on CNBC puts the impact in billions

United States air travel largely returned to normal on Monday after more than 18,000 flight cancellations over three days stemming from Friday’s longest ground stop for 25 years, suspected to have been caused by a single router installed during routine maintenance. Speaking on CNBC, Transportation Secretary Duffy estimated the economic impact of the disruptions, which also delayed nearly 28,000 flights, would be in “billions of dollars.” On Monday, as of 9 a.m. Eastern, there were just 300 flight cancellations and 1,500 delays, down from more than 2,300 canceled and 11,000 delayed on Sunday, according to FlightAware. The four largest airlines face an estimated $345 million earnings hit, according to a brokerage. The Secretary on Friday raised his request for funding for air traffic control and airports to $50 billion from $30 billion; the Administration is still using aging equipment including Compaq computers, floppy disks and paper strips. Democrats in Congress say the Secretary has spent only $1 billion of the initial $12.5 billion approved last year, and want hearings into what led to the disruptions. The Secretary said the system is telegraphing to the American people that it needs investment, and that now is the time to do a big dollar amount to modernize it.

Subjective
NBC News — travel largely returning to normal on Monday, 533 cancelled by 0700, and 68 of Tuesday’s due to be cancelled

Air travel across the United States was largely returning to normal on Monday, although some disruption persisted as airlines scrambled to get back on schedule after the nationwide ground stop. By 7 a.m. Eastern on Monday about 8,365 flights were delayed and 533 cancelled nationwide, a dramatic drop from the 26,392 delayed and 2,858 cancelled flights on Sunday, according to FlightAware. American Airlines had the largest number of canceled flights on Monday at 157, followed by SkyWest with 38; Dallas-Fort Worth and Chicago O’Hare were the origin airports with the highest numbers of cancellations. Just 68 flights were due to be cancelled on Tuesday, as passengers gear up for Thanksgiving travel. The Administration lifted the ground stop at 8:15 p.m. on Friday; it was the longest nationwide halt since September 11, 2001, and the Homeland Security Secretary said authorities had found no evidence of a cyberattack. The contractor had been working on replacing a copper line with a fiber line at a remote site in El Dorado, Arkansas; the Secretary said on Sunday that the replacement triggered problems with another recently replaced router in Amarillo, Texas, which started broadcasting and overloading routers at other centers. The Administration said it still does not know what ultimately caused the problem in maintenance work done thousands of times before without issue.

Subjective
ConsumerAffairs — operations approaching normal on Monday morning, about 250 cancelled by 0400, and the Administration’s Sunday explanation

United States airline operations were moving toward normal on Monday morning, November 16, following a weekend spent recovering from Friday’s nationwide ground stop, although some travelers continued to face canceled flights. About 250 flights were canceled by 4 a.m. Eastern on Monday, according to FlightAware; that follows a Sunday when the tracker recorded 2,291 cancellations as of 3 p.m. American said it did not anticipate additional widespread cancellations tied to the ground stop, and Delta reported progress, saying on Sunday that most flights were operating normally. Friday’s disruption began after a technical problem developed around 3:30 p.m. Eastern; the system stabilized and traffic resumed at 8:15 p.m., nearly five hours later. In an explanation released on Sunday, the Administration said excessive data overwhelmed parts of its telecommunications network, disrupting aircraft communications and radar feeds; investigators identified two potential sources, a radar facility in Amarillo, Texas, and a radio communications site in El Dorado, Arkansas, and the network provider blocked those locations, helping stabilize the network, while the underlying cause continued to be investigated.

Subjective
Reuters — the four largest airlines face a $345 million hit, in a brokerage estimate

The four largest United States airlines face an estimated $345 million earnings hit after the nationwide ground stop on Friday disrupted flights through the weekend, according to a brokerage estimate published on Monday. The estimate puts the cost to American, Delta, United and Southwest at about $345 million pretax combined, with a range of roughly $270 million to $430 million. The Transportation Secretary said on a Sunday programme that operations would probably be fully normal by Monday, as airlines worked to reposition aircraft and crews and restore schedules; earlier on Monday, on CNBC, he urged Congress to swiftly fund air traffic control upgrades after saying the disruption likely caused billions in losses.

Subjective
AsiaToday — China confirms the first Xi-Trump-Putin summit for Thursday at APEC in Shenzhen

China confirmed on Monday that President Xi Jinping will host United States President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin for the first trilateral summit of the three leaders on Thursday, November 19, on the sidelines of this week’s APEC leaders’ meeting in Shenzhen. The 33rd APEC Economic Leaders’ Meeting runs on November 18 and 19, with Xi chairing the gathering of leaders from the forum’s 21 member economies. China’s Foreign Ministry announced the meeting in a brief statement on Monday, giving the date and the venue but no details of the agenda. The White House and the Kremlin had already confirmed the plan, and Beijing’s statement was the first official confirmation from the Chinese side. The three presidents have never met together in a trilateral format before. Discussions are expected to cover global conflicts, artificial intelligence and the reduction of nuclear weapons, according to reporting on the meeting.

Subjective
Silent Dossier — China confirms Xi will host Trump and Putin in Shenzhen, and will not name nuclear arms or Iran as topics

China’s foreign ministry confirmed on Monday, November 16, that Xi Jinping will meet Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump in Shenzhen on Thursday, November 19; it was the host’s first confirmation, three days after the White House announced the meeting and two days after the Kremlin did. “They will exchange views in depth on safeguarding world peace and promoting strategic stability in major-power relations, which is of groundbreaking significance,” spokeswoman Mao Ning told the ministry’s daily briefing; she said it would be the first face-to-face meeting of the three countries’ heads of state. A Japanese reporter then put Washington’s agenda to her, nuclear arms control and Iran; Mao named neither, saying the leaders would exchange views in depth on major issues bearing on global peace and that China would release information in a timely manner. The ministry had given the same holding answer at five briefings between November 4 and 13. The White House said on November 13 that the President will raise nuclear weapons cuts and Iran; a senior official said the same day that no agreement is expected. The United Nations Secretary-General said in Manila on Monday that the United Nations is ready to support a denuclearisation programme and to be fully engaged in it, adding that it is not yet guaranteed the parties will get there, and called on Iran for a serious diplomatic process to end a state of neither peace nor war. The account also carries the German Chancellor’s words from the Dublin meeting of November 13, “Please, no surprises,” addressed to Washington.

Subjective
ABC Audio — the President heads to Asia, leaves Monday morning, and meets the Quad in Manila before Shenzhen

President Trump is traveling to Asia for meetings with global leaders and for his second visit to China for a meeting with President Xi Jinping. He will participate in the first-ever trilateral meeting between the leaders of the United States, China and Russia on the sidelines of the APEC Summit in China, senior officials said. The President is expected to leave Washington on the morning of Monday, November 16, and arrive in Manila on the evening of Tuesday, November 17, and will head to a bilateral meeting with the other members of the Quad, the partnership of the United States with Australia, India and Japan. He is also expected to sign a trade deal with Thailand, participate in an ASEAN cocktail reception followed by a summit dinner, and the next day participate in a welcome ceremony at the presidential palace in Manila and a bilateral meeting there. After Wednesday’s events in the Philippines, the President travels to Shenzhen, China. The trilateral meeting will be the final event on the Asia swing.

Subjective
Candid Dragon — the Monday morning briefing: the President leaves for Asia, a third carrier reaches the Middle East, and Congress gets its first briefing on the stop

The morning briefing for Monday, November 16, checked against at least two outlets or an official source on each item. President Trump leaves Washington today for Manila, where he attends the United States-ASEAN summit on Tuesday, then flies to Shenzhen on Wednesday afternoon; on Thursday he is scheduled to attend the APEC leaders’ session, hold a bilateral meeting with President Xi, and then join Xi and President Putin for the first face-to-face meeting ever among the leaders of the United States, China and Russia. China’s foreign ministry confirmed the meeting on Monday and called it groundbreaking; the Kremlin confirmed the November 19 date over the weekend. Officials say the President wants to talk about cutting nuclear arsenals and about Iran, Ukraine is not expected to come up, and no separate one-on-one with President Putin is scheduled. The briefing also carries a third American carrier reaching the Middle East as Iran claims more sinkings in Hormuz, Congress receiving its first briefing on the ground stop, and a whistleblower interview.

Subjective
The carrier account — a third carrier enters the region, new strikes ‘highly unlikely,’ Tehran still at war, and a drone at Khor Mor

The USS Theodore Roosevelt carrier strike group entered the Central Command area of operations on Sunday, joining the USS George H.W. Bush and the USS George Washington, both already operating in the Arabian Sea, in a force of more than 20 Navy ships enforcing a blockade of Iranian ports; an American official said the three-carrier presence is expected to be temporary as strike groups rotate, though all three could stay if necessary. The Guards said they launched six drones at an American air defence radar system at the Al-Riffa helicopter base in Bahrain on Sunday, describing the strike as a response to American aggression and claiming a successful impact; Bahrain’s military said it intercepted the attacks before they hit their targets. The President told reporters on Sunday that new strikes on Iran are highly unlikely as long as negotiations keep making progress, and that the United States could hit Iran’s nuclear facilities within five minutes if needed. Iran’s deputy foreign minister said in a televised interview that Tehran is preparing for three scenarios—diplomacy, economic blockade and military aggression—and that from a legal perspective Iran is still in a state of war; he listed Iran’s demands as a permanent end to the war on all fronts, removal of the blockade, resolution of the frozen-assets issue, and lifting of certain sanctions including those on oil. Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf said the conflict could end if Washington accepted Iran’s logical conditions and warned that if the United States resumes strikes, Iran’s forces would determine the geography of battle. Separately, a drone struck the Khor Mor gas field in Iraq’s Sulaymaniyah province on Sunday, setting off a large fire and cutting nearly 2,800 megawatts of regional power generation; no group has claimed it, Kurdish officials called it a terrorist attack, and the Iraqi prime minister’s office ordered a joint investigation with the Kurdish authorities. The account also carries the whistleblower complaint filed on Friday by an Army major who survived the March 1 drone attack on the Port Shuaiba command post in Kuwait, and the President’s scheduled Monday meeting in Washington with Qatar’s prime minister.

Subjective
Al Jazeera — Iran says it targets a United States radar in Bahrain: what is known, in order

The Guards say they launched six drones at a United States air defence radar system at Bahrain’s Riffa Air Base in response to what they describe as hostile American actions. Sirens sounded in Bahrain on Sunday as the Interior Ministry urged residents to remain calm and proceed to the nearest safe location; it was the second time in three days that the Guards claimed to have targeted a United States radar system in Bahrain. The Guards said they struck the radar, according to a statement carried by the Fars agency; the Interior Ministry issued two alerts within about three hours, the first at about 4:30 a.m. local time, and the Defence Force said its air defence systems thwarted several Iranian aerial attacks targeting the kingdom. On Friday the Guards said they destroyed a United States early-warning radar system in Bahrain in retaliation for what they described as an air attack on a telecommunications tower in southern Iran; Central Command denied the claim, saying it had shot down two drones and there were no injuries or damage. The American military said it intercepted two Iranian drones on Friday but had yet to comment on Sunday’s claim in the account’s file.

Subjective
Military.com — Iran targets a military base in a second Bahrain drone attack in three days, and the Embassy warns Americans

Iran launched a drone attack against a military base in Bahrain, its second strike on the country in the past three days. The Guards said they used six drones to target the United States air defense radar facility at the al-Riffa air base on Sunday, days after similarly firing drones at Bahrain on Friday. Bahrain’s military said its air defense systems intercepted and destroyed the drones. The base hosts critical American air defense infrastructure, including a key early-warning radar site, and supports American rotary-wing operations. The American Embassy in Bahrain on Sunday warned Americans to exercise heightened vigilance, adding that there could be possible flight cancellations, airspace closures and other travel disruptions after the drone attacks. The American military said it intercepted two Iranian attack drones headed toward Bahrain on Sunday, while the Guards claimed they struck an early warning radar system in the kingdom; the United States denied Iran’s claim. The strikes break a two-month lull in Iranian attacks on Gulf states, testing negotiations aimed at ending the eight-month conflict and reopening the Strait of Hormuz.

Subjective
Crisis Zone — Bahrain says it destroyed Iranian aerial attacks as Tehran claims a radar strike, updated to Monday midday

Bahrain’s Interior Ministry issued its first threat alerts since September, naming no threat, while explosions were heard in Manama; the Defence Force then said its air defences intercepted and destroyed several Iranian aerial attacks. The Guards said six drones targeted an American air-defence radar at the Al-Riffa helicopter base; no damage or casualties had been reported, and neither American nor Bahraini authorities had confirmed any hit. The Guards’ statement was carried by the state broadcaster’s channel, by Fars and by Press TV. Friday’s claim was denied by Central Command, which said two drones were shot down with no injuries or damage. The account, updated on Monday, November 16, records that the American Ambassador to Bahrain said on Sunday that the Guards’ claims were false and that all drones were intercepted, with no damage or injuries reported. The account records the President’s Saturday condition, that he might hold off on attacking Iran if there were no new provocations, and that he would maintain the naval blockade. Monitoring of the story ended at midday on Monday.

Subjective
Trending News Talk — the United States denies Iran destroyed a radar in Bahrain, as two drones are shot down

The United States denied an Iranian claim that a radar system in Bahrain was destroyed, as American forces said they shot down two drones over the Gulf kingdom on Sunday. Iran said its Guards had targeted a United States early warning radar at a military base in Bahrain and destroyed it; American officials rejected that account and said the drones were intercepted before they could cause damage. Bahrain said its air defences had intercepted the incoming aircraft on Sunday, and no casualties were reported in the first accounts. The latest incident followed a similar Iranian claim on November 15, when blasts and sirens sounded across Bahrain in the early hours and residents were told to take shelter. Iran framed both attacks as retaliation for American military action, according to reports carried by Iranian media. The claims could not be independently verified from the scene, and neither American nor Bahraini officials confirmed damage to the installation in their public statements.

Subjective
Action Network — the Alaska Senate race on November 16: the Press’s count at 0840, the markets’ trackers, and the November 18 tabulation

The Alaska Senate race polls had Ms. Peltola and Senator Sullivan within a couple of points, and nearly two weeks after Election Day the Press has still not called the results. As of November 16 at 8:40 a.m. Eastern, the Press’s count shows Ms. Peltola with 140,637 votes, 49.9 percent, and Senator Sullivan with 129,424, 46.0 percent, with an estimated 97 percent of votes counted. One market has the Democrat at 99.8 cents; another market’s tracker lists 92 percent of the vote counted, with Ms. Peltola at 140,640 votes, and a third tracker lists 95.9 percent counted, with the Democratic party at 138,240 votes and the Republican party at 127,828. If no candidate finishes above 50 percent of first-choice votes, Alaska’s ranked-choice tabulation is scheduled for November 18, and certification is targeted for November 25. The Juneau paper reported on Friday night that fewer than 12,000 ballots remained to be counted, and overseas ballots can still arrive through November 18. More Division of Elections updates are due this week. The full count in the Press’s figures: Ms. Peltola 140,637, Senator Sullivan 129,424, Mr. Heikes 6,002, Mr. Daniel J. Sullivan Jr. 4,652 and write-ins 872.

Subjective
Valcore News — Ms. Peltola edges past 50 percent in the count as Senator Sullivan waits

Democrat Mary Peltola has claimed victory in Alaska’s Senate race, the only contest of the midterms still without a projected winner. After Saturday’s count she leads Senator Dan Sullivan by more than 11,000 votes and has nudged just past the 50 percent that would spare her a ranked-choice count; with write-in votes shared out, she has 50.1 percent of first-choice votes to Senator Sullivan’s 46.1 percent, with more than 283,000 ballots counted. On the state’s full summary, which counts write-ins as cast, she sits at 49.94 percent. Senator Sullivan’s spokesman, Mr. Adams, said the campaign was still waiting for every ballot to be counted. Counting continues through Wednesday, Alaska time, the last day for overseas absentee ballots, followed by ranked-choice tabulation if no one has a majority; the Division of Elections aims to certify results by November 25. A victory for Ms. Peltola would give the Democrats a 56-to-44 Senate majority from January.

Subjective
Politix+ — the Alaska results page: Ms. Peltola listed the winner at 50.1 percent

The live Alaska results page lists the United States Senate race as follows: Mary Peltola, 140,637 votes, 50.1 percent, marked the winner; Dan Sullivan, 129,424 votes, 46.11 percent; and Daniel J. Sullivan Jr., 4,652 votes, 1.66 percent. The page carries polling averages as of November 16, 2026.

Subjective
The Apex Wire — Mr. Huang weighs a return as allies lobby the board, and the petition passes 168,000 on Monday

Mr. Huang has discussed returning as Nvidia’s chief executive days after resigning, as allies organise a campaign to press the board and the Treasury Secretary demands a shake-up. He resigned as president, chief executive and a board member in an announcement on November 12; the company’s filing said the board accepted the resignation on November 11. Tesla’s chief, Mr. Musk, and Epic Games’ chief, Mr. Sweeney, were among the executives backing an open letter calling on the board to bring Jensen back. A petition calling for his reinstatement passed 168,000 signatures on Monday, including more than 8,000 current employees and more than 88,000 shareholders, according to its counter. The Treasury Secretary called on Sunday for a dramatic shake-up at the company and an external appointment. Investors Mr. Gerstner and Mr. Baker urged the board to keep a return on the table. The shares fell 13 percent last week, their biggest weekly drop since April 2025; results are due Tuesday, at about 1:20 p.m. Pacific with a call at 2 p.m. No reinstatement has been announced; Mr. Huang has discussed a possible comeback with confidants, the company has not said it is considering reinstating him, and Ms. Kress remains interim chief executive.

Subjective
Traders Union — can Mr. Huang return: petitions, letters, and a behind-the-scenes campaign past 160,000

A campaign called Stand with Jensen has gained momentum; by November 16, a petition demanding Mr. Huang’s reinstatement had gathered more than 160,000 signatures. Mr. Musk, Mr. Sweeney of Epic Games and Mr. Tan of Y Combinator are among the backers; Mr. Musk publicly backed the initiative and said he intended to sign the appeal. The petition’s organizers demand that Mr. Huang be reinstated pending the completion of an independent investigation, or that the board provide convincing evidence that his removal serves the company’s interests. Major shareholders Mr. Gerstner and Mr. Baker sent a separate letter to the board. The shares fell 12.7 percent last week, the worst performance since April 2025. The Treasury Secretary on Sunday urged the company to make a dramatic leadership shakeup and appoint an outside candidate. The board has begun searching for a successor, in the account. The company is scheduled to release its quarterly earnings on Tuesday, November 17, its first presentation since the resignation, with the interim chief expected to answer investors’ questions. The final decision rests with the board, which must take into account the findings of the investigations and pressure from the authorities, in the account.

Subjective
TipRanks — Mr. Huang may return as tech leaders push for his comeback, and the board approached the chief of Arm

Former Nvidia chief Mr. Huang is receiving support from Mr. Musk and other tech leaders for a possible comeback; a group of Silicon Valley executives is forming a war room to urge the board to bring him back. An online petition asking the board to bring him back has received 106,000 signatures in the account’s earlier reading; the petition includes names such as Mr. Kalanick, Mr. Baker, Mr. Lütke of Shopify and Mr. Sweeney of Epic Games. Mr. Musk wrote on Friday that a petition is underway to reinstate Jensen and that he is signing it too. The board had approached the chief of Arm, Mr. Haas, as a potential successor, according to the Financial Times reporting carried in the account. Nvidia is set to report its third-quarter results on Tuesday, November 17, after the market closes; Wall Street expects revenue to jump nearly 91 percent to $108.93 billion from $57.01 billion a year earlier, and earnings to rise about 90 percent to $2.47 per share.

Subjective
The Market Periodical — Nvidia stock on edge as the campaign gains momentum, the letter at 166,322

Nvidia stock faces another test on Monday, November 16, after reports that Mr. Huang wants to return as chief executive, a day before the company’s earnings announcement. A group of Silicon Valley executives is reportedly organizing efforts to persuade the board to reinstate him. According to its website, 166,322 people signed the letter. Mr. Musk, Mr. Masad of Replit, Mr. Sweeney of Epic Games, Mr. Kalanick, Mr. Lütke of Shopify and Mr. Tan of Y Combinator have signed the petition, in the account. It is unclear whether a return will be possible, especially because of pressure from Washington, in the account. Analysts expect the results to show revenue surged by over 90 percent last quarter to $108 billion.

Subjective
Tech & Money Press — chip stocks slide after Taiwan’s 6 percent drop, the Taiex at 41,040.08, and the semiconductor fund down 4.2 percent premarket

Chip stocks started the week under pressure on both sides of the Pacific. Taiwan’s Taiex fell 6.03 percent on Monday, down 2,635.04 points to close at 41,040.08, its second-largest point drop on record; TSMC fell 5.74 percent to NT$2,215 and accounted for about 1,000 points of the drop on its own. South Korea’s Kospi closed down 3.59 percent at 5,100.50 and Japan’s Nikkei 225 fell 2.4 percent to 59,662.02. The semiconductor fund was quoted near $466.23 at 7:24 a.m. Eastern, about 4.2 percent below Friday’s close of $486.75; Nvidia was quoted near $156.41, about 4.0 percent below Friday’s close, and AMD about 5.2 percent lower in the same premarket reading. The sell-off comes one day before Nvidia reports its results, the company’s first report since Mr. Huang resigned. On Tuesday the outlook will matter more than the quarter, in the account; consensus calls for about $109.2 billion in revenue and $2.48 in adjusted earnings per share.

Subjective
The Evergreen Edit — Asian chip stocks tumble and United States futures slip before Nvidia’s earnings

Chip stocks fell sharply across Asia on Monday, November 16: South Korea’s Kospi dropped 3.6 percent, Taiwan’s main index fell 6 percent and Japan’s Nikkei 225 lost 2.4 percent, according to the Press. In Seoul, SK Hynix fell 7.9 percent and Samsung Electronics lost 4.5 percent; in Taiwan, TSMC dropped 5.7 percent. United States stock futures also edged lower on Sunday evening as investors braced for Nvidia’s earnings on Tuesday and a stock market debut later in the week. Nvidia stock fell 4.3 percent on Thursday and another 2 percent on Friday, and lost nearly 13 percent for the week. Nvidia reports results for its fiscal third quarter on Tuesday, November 17, after the market closes; it is the first report under interim chief Ms. Kress.

Subjective
Cointelegraph — Asian chip stocks tumble ahead of Nvidia’s earnings, in the session’s earlier readings

Asian semiconductor stocks slid on Monday ahead of Nvidia’s quarterly earnings. A chip-testing equipment maker dropped about 10.4 percent, an inspection equipment maker declined more than 10.7 percent and a chipmaking equipment supplier fell 5.7 percent, according to the finance data carried in the account. South Korean memory makers Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix lost 5.8 percent and 4.2 percent respectively in the account’s session readings, while TSMC slipped 3.8 percent; the broad decline came amid a wider sell-off in regional markets, with Japan’s Nikkei 225 down 2 percent and South Korea’s Kospi losing 2.6 percent as of 4:04 a.m. UTC. In August, Nvidia forecast third-quarter revenue of $108 billion, plus or minus 2 percent, excluding any data center compute revenue from China; analysts expect slightly higher quarterly revenue of $109.3 billion, including $101.8 billion from its data center business, in the account. Nvidia shares closed Friday down 2.01 percent at $162.85.

Subjective
Desk Notes — Nasdaq futures slide 1.27 percent as Nvidia’s earnings loom and the chairman speaks at noon

Monday, November 16: technology leads futures lower at the start of a week built around one report. At 7:07 a.m. Eastern, Nasdaq 100 futures were at 27,679.75, down 355 points or 1.27 percent; S&P 500 futures were at 7,540.50, down 42.50 or 0.56 percent; and Dow futures were at 52,398, down 20 or 0.04 percent. Nvidia shares were at $157.07 pre-market at 7:18 a.m., down $5.78 or 3.55 percent from Friday’s close of $162.85; the stock has fallen for six straight weeks. The volatility index stood at 20.55, up 1.25 points or 6.48 percent, at 7:17 a.m.; the ten-year Treasury yielded 5.127 percent at 7:17 a.m. Friday in one line: the S&P 500 fell 0.40 percent to 7,561.67 as chip stocks sold off. On the calendar: the New York manufacturing index for November at 8:30 a.m., consensus 18 after 25.5; the chairman’s remarks at noon; and on Tuesday, Nvidia’s earnings, October retail sales at 8:30 a.m. with consensus 0.2 percent after 0.8 percent, and industrial production at 9:15 a.m.

Subjective
Finnhub — Nvidia’s market data on Monday morning: $159.55 at 1053 Eastern, against Friday’s close of $162.85

The market-data page for Nvidia on Monday, November 16, shows the market in regular session, opened at 9:30 a.m. Eastern, with the latest available price at $159.55 as of 10:53:44 a.m. Eastern. The quote snapshot for the trading date shows an open of $159.015, a high of $163.2, a low of $158.11, a previous close of $162.85, and a reported change of minus $3.30, or minus 2.0264 percent. Recent sessions: November 13 opened at $169.905 and closed at $162.85; November 12 opened at $151.005 and closed at $166.19. The page puts the market value at $3.92 trillion, the five-session return at minus 14.51 percent, and the third-quarter estimate, for November 17, at earnings of $2.523 per share on revenue of $111.203 billion in its table.

Subjective
InvestingLive — gold slips toward $3,876 ahead of the chairman, as the speakers line up behind tighter policy

Gold slipped to around $3,876 in Asia, extending a slide of almost 7 percent since last Tuesday. The Chairman gives opening remarks at the Productivity and Jobs Task Force Conference at 12:00 p.m. Eastern on Monday, hosted by the San Francisco Fed; the forum brings together technology executives, economists and employers to examine whether artificial intelligence will lower inflation, push prices higher or displace workers. The Chairman has staked part of his leadership on the idea that artificial intelligence can ease inflation, and on Monday he makes that case to colleagues who have spent the past few days warning it is doing the opposite; Mr. Schmid, Ms. Collins and Mr. Jefferson all stressed persistent inflation in recent remarks, and Mr. Jefferson cited price growth at 3.6 percent. Markets are fully priced for a quarter-point hike on December 8-9. Opening remarks at a themed conference may carry little direct policy guidance, and the Chairman said in October that he does not prejudge meetings; any comment on artificial intelligence’s effect on inflation will be read for clues about December, in the account. The minutes follow on Wednesday.

Subjective
Ad Hoc News — the chairman’s dilemma: why gold traders are listening to a technology speech for rate cues, gold at $3,861.43

Gold changed hands at $3,861.43 an ounce, extending a soft patch driven by a firmer dollar and hawkish signals from the Federal Reserve. The Chairman is due to address a public forum in San Francisco, where he will examine artificial intelligence’s implications for inflation, employment and growth across several panel discussions bracketed by his own remarks; no monetary policy decision is scheduled. He initially viewed artificial intelligence as a potential source of stronger productivity and lower inflation; he has since given more weight to the near-term strains created by rolling out the technology, in the account. Governors Cook and Barr have flagged possible job losses from artificial intelligence, with Mr. Barr tying the scale of any disruption to how fast and widely the technology is adopted. The minutes of the October meeting are due on Wednesday, November 18.

Subjective
TheStreet — rate hike fears grow ahead of the December meeting, and the chairman steps into the artificial intelligence universe

The Kansas City president kicked off a busy week of central bank speeches on November 15 by saying that inflation pressures have only grown worse in recent months, leaving policymakers with more work ahead; in addition to him, six officials are scheduled to speak this week. The Chairman is stepping into the heart of the artificial intelligence universe on November 16 while hosting a conference in Silicon Valley to examine whether generative artificial intelligence will spark unprecedented productivity or trigger financial instability and job disruption. The bank’s biggest concern, in the account: whether artificial intelligence will transform the economy with higher productivity and wages or doom it through rising inflation, financial instability and massive job losses. The Chairman has vowed that the bank is committed to the price stability side of its mandate, which has been above its 2 percent target for nearly six years. The New York president, who said on November 12 that inflation is far too high and that further tightening will be needed, also speaks on November 16 as well as the following two days; he suggested that over the medium term, widespread adoption of the technology should boost efficiency and help lower production costs.

Subjective
Demócrata — Russia sees in the Union’s messages a lack of willingness to promote peace, and the commissioners prepare a major exchange

Russian authorities indicated on Monday that the latest European Union statements about negotiations concerning Ukraine suggest a reluctance to contribute to the peace process, although they underlined that Moscow continues to hope to hear directly from the Europeans how its position can help in those diplomatic efforts. The Kremlin’s spokesman recalled that the Commission’s president and her colleagues in Brussels have stated that unconditional support for Ukraine will be maintained and that the bloc will maintain the line of increasing pressure on Russia in order to force it to participate in the peace process. The spokesman also pointed out that so far the negotiations have been coordinated in a trilateral format, referring to contacts between Moscow, Washington and Kyiv, and insisted that Russia does not want a temporary truce, but rather a peace that will last for many years and centuries. The statements come after the Commission’s president reiterated on Sunday that Europe will participate actively in the peace talks through the E5 + EU format—the institutions alongside Germany, France, the United Kingdom, Italy and Poland—while guaranteeing maximum support for Kyiv and maximum pressure on Moscow. The heads of state and government of the Twenty-Seven agreed on Friday at the Dublin summit to set the European negotiating team in motion. The American envoys said after their recent meetings in Moscow and Dublin that Washington is working to incorporate the European partners directly into the next round of trilateral talks, although the Russian Foreign Ministry has questioned whether the Kremlin has given its approval for that participation. Meanwhile, the Russian human-rights commissioner confirmed on Monday that contacts are being maintained with her Ukrainian counterpart with a view to a major exchange of prisoners of war and to organizing a humanitarian mission in Kostiantynivka: “We are in regular contact and we are preparing a major exchange, which has been announced.”

Subjective
European Global Times — Europe picks a five-nation team for the Ukraine talks, and no negotiators have been named

European leaders have settled on a negotiating team for possible seats at the American-brokered Russia-Ukraine peace talks. The president of the European Council announced the decision after an informal summit in Dublin on Friday: Britain, France, Germany, Italy and Poland, the E5 bloc, will represent Europe, alongside envoys from the Commission and the Council. The outcome defied calls from Washington, Kyiv and Moscow for a single European envoy. No negotiators have been named; the five states are likely to field national security advisers rather than heads of government, and it is still unclear who will speak for the institutions, in the account. The deal comes on the heels of the talks in Abu Dhabi, where European officials held separate discussions but were shut out of the core negotiations; the American envoys then met the Russian President in Moscow and the Ukrainian leader in Dublin, and announced that both sides had agreed to bring Europe into the next round. Moscow has not confirmed European participation, in the account. No date has been fixed for the new talks, but the Kremlin’s spokesman said on Friday they will happen fairly soon, probably in Abu Dhabi again, in the account.

Subjective
Reuters — Spain’s right retains a firm poll lead despite Socialist gains, in three polls published on Monday

Madrid, November 16. Spain’s conservative People’s Party and Vox would together win a parliamentary majority in the November 29 election, three opinion polls published on Monday showed, though Prime Minister Sánchez’s Socialists gained ground. The surveys are the first since last week’s campaign launch, which has focused on housing affordability, immigration, corruption and last month’s deadly train crash. A daily poll showed the Socialists rising to 30.3 percent from 29.9 percent, exceeding the 30 percent mark for the first time in that poll since the 2023 election; the People’s Party, on 31.5 percent, and Vox, on 18 percent, would together win more than 190 seats in the 350-seat lower house, a majority. A second poll projected 201 to 205 seats for the two parties combined, and 102 to 104 for the Socialists, whose support rose half a percentage point to 26.1 percent. A third poll showed Socialist support up one percentage point from a week earlier to 26.9 percent, with the right bloc winning 194 seats to the Socialists’ 109. The state poll remained a major outlier: last week it projected 134 to 143 seats for the Socialists against 155 to 171 for the People’s Party and Vox combined, suggesting the Prime Minister could retain power through a broad left-wing coalition.

Subjective
Demócrata — the survey of November 16: both large parties rise, Vox loses four seats, and the right maintains the majority

The start of the November 29 campaign reinforces the two major parties without altering the parliamentary majority the study attributes to the People’s Party and Vox. The fourth wave of the study, with fieldwork carried out between November 10 and 13 and published on November 16, places the Conservatives at 31.5 percent of the votes and the Socialists at 26.9 percent. The People’s Party gains 1.7 points and two seats, to 128; the Socialists recover one point and three representatives, to 109; Vox drops from 19.9 percent to 19.0 percent and from 70 to 66 seats. The two right parties together stand at 194 seats, against 176 needed for a majority.

Subjective
Particle News — the fifth Saturday at 106,000, the police bill to the Senate, and a strike on Tuesday

The nationwide demonstrations ran for a fifth Saturday in a row on November 14 and the Interior Ministry put turnout at about 106,000 people, including roughly 24,000 in Paris, while organisers gave higher estimates. The movement now unites high-school students, trade unions, Yellow Vest activists and child-protection campaigners demanding better school conditions, higher pay and relief from the rising cost of living. At the centre of the protests is a bill passed by the lower house that would give officers a presumption of legitimate self-defence when they use firearms, a measure opponents call a licence to kill in the account’s words, that they say would weaken accountability. With the Senate vote pending and unions rejecting a 0.6 percent minimum-wage offer, the protests threaten to reshape law-and-order debates ahead of the 2027 presidential race, in the account’s reading, and raise the risk of further strikes and clashes next week. Senate consideration of the contested measure is set to follow union plans for a nationwide strike on Tuesday, November 17.

entry.title: Beijing Confirms the Three Presidents for Thursday in Shenzhen, the Airlines Open Monday With 55 Flights Cancelled Against the Fully-Normal Promise, and Asia Sells the Chip Stocks Ahead of Nvidia's Report While Alaska's Count Still Waits
entry.summary: Beijing confirms three presidents for Thursday in Shenzhen, and the airlines open Monday with 55 flights cancelled against a normal promise.
entry.content:
The Night File — The Desk’s Report

Objective

Beijing Confirms the Three Presidents for Thursday in Shenzhen, the Airlines Open Monday With 55 Flights Cancelled Against the Fully-Normal Promise, and Asia Sells the Chip Stocks Ahead of Nvidia’s Report While Alaska’s Count Still Waits

The night file: the host’s confirmation completes the Shenzhen meeting from all three sides; a recovery morning counted at 55 cancellations before it begins; a third carrier in the Gulf and a gas field struck in Iraq; a Senate count that spent the night where Saturday left it; a petition past 160,000 in one account with the board still silent; and an Asian session that sold the chipmakers from Taipei to Seoul.

By Eunice, the desk · Collected and analyzed at 0400 ET, Monday, November 16, 2026. This edition continues the file from Edition No. 53, the Midnight Watch, collected at 0000 today, from Edition No. 52, the Evening Watch, collected at 1800 on Sunday, from Edition No. 50, the Midday Watch, collected at 1200 on Sunday, and from Edition No. 49, the Overnight Watch, collected at 0400 on Sunday. Those editions stand unrevised, as a log stands. Where the overnight figures differ from the earlier figures, the difference is stated here, in the open.

The Night in Brief: A Meeting Completed, a Recovery Opened, and No Count Moved

The night completed one meeting, opened one recovery, and moved no count. Beijing’s confirmation, carried in the confirmation account filed below, makes the Shenzhen session of Thursday official from all three capitals, two days after the White House announced it and one after the Kremlin confirmed it. The airlines’ Monday stands at 55 flights cancelled as of Sunday evening in the wire account filed below, the smallest opening figure of the four days, against the Secretary’s promise that the system would be probably fully normal on Monday. The Gulf gained a third American carrier and a struck gas field in Iraq and no word on the radar at Al-Riffa. Alaska’s count did not move in the night; its next count is due today. The petition for Mr. Huang passed 160,000 signatures in the Seoul account filed below, and the board’s answer is still not in the file. Asia opened the week by selling the chip stocks, Taiwan’s index closing down 6.0 percent in the closing account filed below. The desk takes the files in that order.

What the night settled is short: the meeting is confirmed, Monday’s cancellations are counted in the dozens and not the thousands, and every dated thing on the calendar—Mr. Warsh at noon, the count in Juneau, the President’s departure—still stands where Sunday left it. What it left open is the rest of the file: the root cause, the radar, the call, and the board.

The Airlines at 0400: Monday Opens at 55 Cancelled, Sunday’s Finals Stand Apart, and the Itemized Request Is Due Today

Monday opens with the smallest number of the four days, and the desk prints the three counts of it that the night carried. As of Sunday evening, 55 flights within, into or out of the United States scheduled for Monday were cancelled, in the wire account above; an earlier Sunday-afternoon count put Monday’s cancellations at 144, in the timeline account filed below; and the tracker account filed with the midnight edition counted 33 on Sunday afternoon. The three readings were taken at different hours of the same afternoon and evening, and they agree on the order of the day: a normal Monday schedule carries cancellations in the dozens, and Sunday closed in the thousands.

Sunday’s own final figures stand apart in the same file and are printed in the cocked hat: more than 2,300 cancelled in the Reuters count carried at midnight, more than 1,960 in the wire account above, and 18,689 delays in the timeline account against some 7,700 in the wire’s. No second stop was ordered in the night, and no Administration statement after the Secretary’s Sunday programmes stands in the overnight file.

The cause file gained two sentences and no answer. Two people familiar with the investigation said the router installation itself went smoothly, and that a detailed procedure of each step of the process is submitted to the Administration, in the Reuters account filed below. Both routers are with L3Harris, the contractor that owns and operates the network, while Administration staff are on site and the Federal Bureau of Investigation is offering support, in the El Dorado account filed below; the contractor said in a statement on Saturday that it was cooperating with the review and took the stop’s impact on travellers, airlines and operations seriously, in the same account’s file. The money file waits on Monday: the Secretary said a full, itemized request would be detailed Monday, in the Washington reporting carried in the El Dorado account; his Thursday letter to lawmakers asked for $30.1 billion, in the same account, against the $50 billion he has sought since Friday and the $12.5 billion approved last year, of which two House members say about $11 billion remains unspent. Settled: Monday’s opening count. Open: the root cause, in the Secretary’s own Sunday words, and the itemized request.

The Gulf at 0400: A Third Carrier in the Region, ‘Highly Unlikely’ From the President, a State of War From Tehran, and a Gas Field Struck in Iraq

The Gulf’s night was naval and verbal. The USS Theodore Roosevelt carrier strike group entered the Central Command area on Sunday, joining the USS George H.W. Bush and the USS George Washington in the Arabian Sea—three carriers in the region, in a force of more than 20 ships enforcing the blockade of Iranian ports—in the carrier account filed below, which records that the presence is expected to be temporary as strike groups rotate and that all three could stay if necessary.

The words matched the deployment in both directions. The President told reporters on Sunday that new strikes on Iran are ‘highly unlikely’ as long as negotiations keep making progress, and that the United States could hit Iran’s nuclear facilities ‘within five minutes’ if needed, in the same account. Tehran’s deputy foreign minister, Mr. Gharibabadi, said in a televised interview that Iran is preparing for three scenarios—diplomacy, economic blockade and military aggression—and that ‘from a legal perspective, we are still in a state of war,’ in the same account; his list of demands stands there whole: a permanent end to the war on all fronts, removal of the blockade, the frozen assets resolved, and sanctions lifted, including on oil. Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf said the conflict could end if Washington accepted Iran’s ‘logical conditions’ and warned that if the United States resumes strikes, Iran’s forces would ‘determine the geography of battle,’ in the same account.

Two claims in the file gained no assessment in the night. On the radar at Al-Riffa, the file stands where midnight left it: six drones in the Guards’ account, intercepts in Manama’s, no impacts to American forces in the Central Command spokesman’s sentence, and no word from any capital on the radar itself. In Iraq, a drone struck the Khor Mor gas field in Sulaymaniyah province on Sunday, setting off a large fire and cutting nearly 2,800 megawatts of regional generation; no group has claimed it, Kurdish officials called it a terrorist attack, and the Iraqi prime minister’s office ordered a joint investigation with the Kurdish authorities, in the carrier account. In Hormuz, the Guards’ claim that two tankers struck mines and that a supertanker carrying more than two million barrels sank stands unconfirmed in every account; a British monitor cited a report from Indian shipping authorities of a tanker attacked in the Gulf on November 15, its crew safe and accounted for, with no details of damage, in the maritime account filed below—an attack confirmed, a sinking not.

One Washington paper joined the file in the night. An Army major who survived the March 1 drone attack on the Port Shuaiba command post in Kuwait, which killed six American soldiers, filed a whistleblower complaint with the House and Senate Armed Services Committees on Friday alleging that senior Army officials ignored warnings and failed to plan for anti-drone defences, in the carrier account; the Secretary of Defense said the day after that attack that the troops there were well protected, in the same account. The allegations are one officer’s, and no finding stands in the file.

Shenzhen at 0400: The Host Confirms, the Agendas Still Differ, and the Road Runs Through Manila

The meeting is now confirmed from all three sides, and the night’s largest fact is a confirmation. China’s Foreign Ministry said on Monday that President Xi will host a meeting of the heads of state of China, Russia and the United States in Shenzhen on Thursday, November 19, in the confirmation account above. The White House announced the plan on Friday through a communications official, Ms. Wales; the Kremlin confirmed on Saturday that the three countries had agreed to hold the summit; Beijing had said only that it was in communication with the relevant parties until Monday’s statement, in the same account.

The agendas still do not match, and the desk prints them side by side. Washington’s stated agenda starts with controlling and reducing nuclear arsenals and takes in the war in Iran; a senior American official told the Press the session is meant to begin a conversation on nuclear disarmament, with no agreement expected, in the confirmation account. The same official said Ukraine will not be discussed at the three-way session; the Kremlin aide, Mr. Ushakov, said on November 12 that the Ukraine settlement would be discussed with the President in Shenzhen, in the same account. No separate meeting between the President and President Putin is planned, in the same account; bilateral talks and a working lunch with President Xi stand on Thursday ahead of the three-way session.

The road to the room runs through Manila, and it begins today. The President is scheduled to leave Washington on Monday, attend the ASEAN summit in the Philippines on November 17, and travel to Shenzhen for the APEC leaders’ meeting of November 18 and 19, which President Xi chairs, in the confirmation account and in the itinerary account filed below. In Manila he will meet the leaders of India, Japan and Australia in a Quad summit on Tuesday, sign a trade deal with Thailand, and receive a state visit welcome on Wednesday, in the itinerary account. One American account notes what will travel with him: the matter of Mr. Huang’s chips will loom over the visit to Shenzhen, and American officials have said the President does not intend to raise the spying matter with President Xi, in the trip account filed below. Before he leaves, the President is scheduled to meet Qatar’s prime minister in Washington on Monday, in the carrier account filed above; Qatar has been stepping up its efforts to broker an end to the war.

Europe at 0400: A Channel Opened From Washington, No Call From Brussels, and Two Sentences From Moscow Unamended

Europe’s file gained a channel and no call. Mr. Kushner said in a social media post over the weekend that Russia and Ukraine had agreed to expand participation in the next round of talks to include European partners, in the force account filed below; an American account of the channel describes the focus of the diplomacy now as bringing Moscow and Europe into direct engagement and preparing the agenda for the next round of the trilateral talks, in the channel account filed below. No date, venue or format for direct Europe-to-Russia talks has been announced, in the same account.

Moscow’s two Sunday sentences stand unamended at 0400. The negotiators Europe has chosen have not yet attempted to make contact with Russia, the spokesman told the TASS agency, in the force account; and in the interview with a Vesti correspondent he said the settlement in Ukraine will be linked to a new security architecture on the European continent—‘two component parts, and neither can exist without the other’—and that absent a negotiated solution Russia will have to achieve its objectives by force, in the same accounts. Europe’s stated position, from the Council President, Mr. Costa, is that only Ukraine has the legitimacy to decide on matters concerning its territory and sovereignty, in the channel account. The next fact in this file is a telephone call that has not been made.

Alaska’s count spent the night exactly where Saturday afternoon left it, and the overnight file adds an explanation and a spokesman, not a number. Alaska’s count resumes ahead of Wednesday’s tabulation. Mr. Warsh speaks at noon. The President meets Qatar’s prime minister in Washington and then departs for Manila. The Clippings Filed With This Edition

Everything the desk read for the report above, clipped and filed as a bureau files it. Each item is stamped subjective—a source with a position, printed because it is useful—and described by what it says. The desk’s report is the only item in this edition stamped objective. 29 items.

Subjective
The wire account — a return to normal expected on Monday, and 55 of Monday’s flights cancelled as of Sunday evening

United States air travel was expected to return to normal on Monday after three days of widespread disruption following the no-takeoff order issued on Friday. As of Sunday evening, more than 55 flights within, into or out of the United States scheduled for Monday were cancelled, according to the tracker FlightAware, a dramatic shift from the more than 1,960 flights cancelled on Sunday in the same account. The ground stop issued on Friday afternoon was only the second such nationwide directive since the September 11 attacks and was blamed on faulty work to upgrade air traffic control communication cables. The Administrator had said on Saturday that travel would return to normal by the close of business on Sunday; the Secretary said on Sunday morning it would take longer to get planes, crews and travellers where they need to be, and that the system would be probably fully normal on Monday.

Subjective
The timeline account — 9,000 cancelled on Friday, 144 of Monday’s down as of Sunday afternoon, and the routers at El Dorado and Amarillo

The Administration grounded departing flights at every United States airport on Friday, November 13, from 3:54 p.m. Eastern, with about 3,500 aircraft in the air, until the stop was lifted at 8:15 p.m. About 9,000 flights were cancelled on Friday, roughly 6,400 more on Saturday, and cancellations carried into Sunday, when about 2,300 flights were cancelled and 18,689 delayed, according to FlightAware. Officials say the cause was network equipment, not a cyberattack: routers at Administration sites in El Dorado, Arkansas, and Amarillo, Texas, flooded air traffic control systems with data during a copper-to-fiber upgrade, and the root cause is still being investigated. The Administrator says there is zero evidence of anything nefarious. Cancellations for Monday fell sharply, with 144 reported as of Sunday afternoon, and airlines expect near-normal operations on Monday with occasional knock-on cancellations possible.

Subjective
The Apex Wire — 55 of Monday’s flights pre-cancelled, three days past 18,000, and the Administration’s Friday figure of 12,462

United States air travel returns to normal on Monday after three days of disruption, with only about 55 Monday flights cancelled after more than 18,000 cancellations across the three days. The Administration lifted its nationwide ground stop at about 8:30 p.m. Eastern on Friday, ending a halt of about four and a half hours; more than 25,000 flights were delayed by 9:30 p.m. Friday, according to FlightAware. More than 6,150 flights were cancelled on Saturday and more than 7,300 delayed; Sunday brought more than 2,300 cancellations and about 7,700 delays, taking the three-day total past 18,000. The Administration later said operators cancelled about 12,462 flights on Friday, including 9,082 by major airlines, though not all were directly caused by the ground stop, and 827 flights were diverted. The stop was ordered after a telecommunications outage struck the air traffic control system, affecting all 22 Air Route Traffic Control Centers.

Subjective
Reuters — more than 11,500 flights affected on Sunday, the installation went smoothly in two accounts, and the $50 billion request

United States air travel disruptions continued for a third day with more than 11,500 flights affected on Sunday, but the Transportation Secretary predicted a return to normalcy by Monday as airlines scrambled to get back on schedule following the systemwide ground stop. The Secretary said on a Sunday programme that there was no evidence of a cyberattack or other malicious intent, but the cause remained unclear, and that flights would come back to normal on Sunday but probably fully normal on Monday. The installation by the contractor L3Harris of at least one new router at a remote facility led to a situation in which other centers were overloaded with a flood of data; the replacement of a router at El Dorado, Arkansas, triggered problems with a recently replaced router in Amarillo, Texas, which started broadcasting and overloading routers at other centers. The functionality of the originating routers has been disabled, as was done for about 60 similar routers. The routers were purchased in 2001 and were obsolete by 2006. Two people familiar with the investigation said the router installation itself went smoothly, and that a detailed procedure of each step of the process is submitted to the Administration. The Secretary has called since Friday for $50 billion to upgrade the systems, up from $30 billion, after Congress approved $12.5 billion last year; two House members answered that about $11 billion of that sum remains unspent.

Subjective
SourceFirst News — both routers with L3Harris, the Bureau offering support, and a Thursday letter that asked for $30.1 billion

Friday’s nationwide ground stop began when a newly installed router at a remote Administration site in El Dorado, Arkansas, started flooding the air traffic control network, the Transportation Secretary said on Sunday; officials still do not know whether the fault lay with the equipment or with the contractor that installed it. The Secretary said a second problem turned up at a radar site in Amarillo, Texas, where work had been done weeks earlier. Both routers are now with L3Harris, the contractor that owns and operates the network, while Administration staff are on site and the Federal Bureau of Investigation is offering support. Investigators are checking whether L3Harris installed the router wrongly or the device itself was faulty, and why the Amarillo site also started causing problems. The contractor owns the network that links the control facilities with remote radar sites and weather stations for voice and data. The Administrator said router swaps of this kind are routine and are not part of the $12.5 billion modernization effort Congress funded last year. The Secretary wants $50 billion in all and says last year’s money covers radar, radios and control centers but not telecom or software; a letter he and the budget director sent lawmakers on Thursday asked for $30.1 billion. The President broke his silence on the ground stop on Sunday by blaming the prior administration and urging Congress to pay for upgrading air traffic control. A governor said on Saturday that the Secretary must resign or be removed and called for a congressional investigation.

Subjective
The carrier account — a third carrier enters the region, new strikes ‘highly unlikely,’ Tehran still at war, and a drone at Khor Mor

The USS Theodore Roosevelt carrier strike group entered the Central Command area of operations on Sunday, joining the USS George H.W. Bush and the USS George Washington, both already operating in the Arabian Sea, in a force of more than 20 Navy ships enforcing a blockade of Iranian ports; an American official said the three-carrier presence is expected to be temporary as strike groups rotate, though all three could stay if necessary. The Guards said they launched six drones at an American air defence radar system at the Al-Riffa helicopter base in Bahrain on Sunday, describing the strike as a response to American aggression and claiming a successful impact; Bahrain’s military said it intercepted the attacks before they hit their targets. The President told reporters on Sunday that new strikes on Iran are ‘highly unlikely’ as long as negotiations keep making progress, and that the United States could hit Iran’s nuclear facilities ‘within five minutes’ if needed. Iran’s deputy foreign minister, Mr. Gharibabadi, said in a televised interview that Tehran is preparing for three scenarios—diplomacy, economic blockade and military aggression—and that from a legal perspective Iran is still in a state of war; he listed Iran’s demands as a permanent end to the war on all fronts, removal of the blockade, resolution of the frozen-assets issue, and lifting of certain sanctions including those on oil. Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf said the conflict could end if Washington accepted Iran’s ‘logical conditions’ and warned that if the United States resumes strikes, Iran’s forces would ‘determine the geography of battle.’ Separately, a drone struck the Khor Mor gas field in Iraq’s Sulaymaniyah province on Sunday, setting off a large fire and cutting nearly 2,800 megawatts of regional power generation; no group has claimed it, Kurdish officials called it a terrorist attack, and the Iraqi prime minister’s office ordered a joint investigation with the Kurdish authorities. An Army major who survived the March 1 drone attack on the Port Shuaiba command post in Kuwait, which killed six American soldiers, filed a whistleblower complaint with the House and Senate Armed Services Committees on Friday alleging that senior Army officials ignored warnings and failed to plan for anti-drone defences; the Secretary of Defense told a press conference the day after that attack that the troops there were well protected. The President is scheduled to meet Qatar’s prime minister in Washington on Monday, and Qatar has been stepping up efforts to broker an end to the war.

Subjective
ASEAN NOW — six drones fired at the base in Bahrain, the second attempt in three days after a lull of two months

Iran has launched a drone attack on a United States military base in Bahrain, its second attempt to target the Gulf state in three days, as its stand-off with the United States over the Strait of Hormuz escalates. The Guards said they targeted the American air defence radar facility at the al-Riffa air base using six drones. Bahrain’s military said its air defence systems intercepted and destroyed the attacks before they reached their targets. The attack follows Iranian drones fired at Bahrain on Friday, Tehran’s first attack against Gulf countries since September; the American military said both of Friday’s drones were shot down with no injuries or damage, denying an Iranian claim to have struck an American early warning radar system.

Subjective
Salaamedia — four capitals condemn the attack on Bahrain, and Tehran rejects a compensation demand

Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Jordan and Egypt condemned Iran’s drone attack on Bahrain on Sunday and expressed solidarity with the kingdom. It was the second attack in three days, after two drones were intercepted at dawn on Friday. Bahrain’s defence forces said their air defence systems intercepted the drones before Iran could achieve its goals, and accused Tehran of a systematic hostile approach. The kingdom issued its first nationwide public safety alert since September, urging residents to move to the nearest safe location. The Guards said they launched six drones at a radar at a United States defence site at the al-Riffa helicopter base, in retaliation for hostile American actions. At his weekly press conference in Tehran on Sunday, Iran’s Foreign Ministry spokesman, Mr. Baghaei, rejected a demand by the Gulf Cooperation Council that Iran pay compensation for its attacks.

Subjective
Seatrade Maritime — a tanker attack confirmed by a monitor with the crew safe, and a claimed sinking with no vessel in the footage

An attack on a tanker in the Arabian Gulf has been confirmed while Iran claims two vessels struck mines in Hormuz, including a very large crude carrier which it says sank. The British maritime monitor cited a report from Indian shipping authorities that a tanker was attacked in the Arabian Gulf as it was approaching the Strait of Hormuz on November 15; the crew were reported safe and accounted for, and there were no details of damage. The Guards claimed two tankers struck mines in the southern corridor of the strait, suffering massive explosions during what it described as unauthorised transits, and that a supertanker carrying over 2 million barrels of crude sank in the southern Gulf. The Guards posted video of the supposed sunken tanker on fire; the account records that there is no discernible vessel in the footage, a large fire and smoke billowing on water. The Iranians did not identify either vessel, and there has been no independent verification of the claimed attacks.

Subjective
Global Insight — the Guards claim a supertanker sunk on a mine, and no independent confirmation has arrived

Iran says a supertanker carrying more than two million barrels of crude oil has sunk in the Persian Gulf after striking a naval mine in the Strait of Hormuz. The claim, made by the Revolutionary Guard on Sunday, November 15, is presented in two columns: in the first, the Guard has formally claimed, in a statement carried by state television and reported by Al Arabiya and Gulf News, that two oil tankers travelling along an unauthorised route in the southern part of the strait struck naval mines, resulting in massive explosions and fire, and that one of them—a super tanker carrying over two million barrels of crude—sank in the southern waters of the Gulf. The Guard did not name either vessel, give their flags or owners, or provide casualty figures. In the second column: no independent source has confirmed either incident. The British maritime monitor said the damage and environmental impact were unknown but the crew were safe. The account’s standing rule is printed with it: claims from a party to a conflict need independent corroboration before they can be treated as fact, and that corroboration has not arrived.

Subjective
TML — China confirms the Shenzhen meeting on Monday, and the confirmations stand complete from all three sides

China’s Foreign Ministry confirmed on Monday, November 16, that President Xi Jinping will host a trilateral meeting with President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen on Thursday, November 19. The session, on the sidelines of the APEC summit, is the first time the three leaders have met together, and Washington says nuclear arms cuts and the Iran war are on its agenda. The White House announced the plan on Friday, November 13, through a communications official, Ms. Wales, and the Kremlin spokesman confirmed on Saturday, November 14, that the three countries had agreed to hold the summit; Beijing, the host, had said only that it was in communication with the relevant parties until Monday’s statement. The meeting takes place on the sidelines of the 33rd APEC Summit, which China is hosting in Shenzhen on November 18 and 19, with President Xi chairing the leaders’ meeting of the forum’s 21 member economies. The President is also expected to hold bilateral talks and a working lunch with President Xi on November 19, and Washington says there is no plan for a separate meeting between the President and President Putin. A senior American official told the Press the session is meant to begin a conversation on nuclear disarmament, with no agreement expected, and said Ukraine will not be discussed at the three-way session; a Kremlin aide said on November 12 that the Ukraine settlement would be discussed with the President in Shenzhen. The President’s route to the room runs through Manila: he is scheduled to leave Washington on Monday, November 16, attend the ASEAN Summit in the Philippines on November 17, and then travel to Shenzhen for APEC and the trilateral session.

Subjective
The Associated Press, carried by KXL — the President departs Monday, a trade deal with Thailand in Manila, and nuclear talks in Shenzhen

President Donald Trump is preparing to depart for Asia on Monday, turning his focus to economic deals and historic three-way nuclear talks with Russia and China as his administration adjusts to a new political reality in Washington. His trip begins in Manila and continues to the Chinese tech hub of Shenzhen. In the Philippines, the President will meet Southeast Asian leaders and plans to sign a trade deal with Thailand while in Manila, the White House said. He then heads to China for the APEC summit and, at the end of the trip, the first-ever three-way talks with China’s President Xi and Russia’s President Putin to discuss nuclear stockpiles. The President and American officials have indicated that the meeting will focus on nuclear weapons and that topics of discussion would not include Russia’s war in Ukraine, now in its fifth year.

Subjective
CNN — the Asia trip as an attempt to reassert authority, and the Huang matter travelling with it to Shenzhen

President Donald Trump will attempt to reassert his authority this week with a long-planned trip through Asia, punctuated Thursday by an unprecedented three-way meeting with his counterparts from China and Russia. The scandal involving Mr. Huang’s AI chips will loom over the President’s visit to Shenzhen, the hub of China’s tech industry; the President does not intend to raise the spying matter with President Xi, with whom he will meet for the fourth time in just over a year, American officials have previously told the network. The President departs for the Philippines on Monday after shaking up his West Wing leadership and facing calls even from some allies to fire members of his Cabinet. At the ASEAN summit in Manila and the APEC summit in Shenzhen he will look to counter the narrative of declining power by announcing new commercial deals and asserting American presence in the region. President Putin originally proposed the three-party summit as a venue to discuss the Ukraine war; the President’s aides insist Thursday’s meeting is nothing of the sort, and say Ukraine will not even be on the agenda. President Xi had initially appeared skeptical of hosting the meeting, officials said, concerned it could overshadow the APEC summit.

Subjective
ANI, carried by Daily Prabhat — the itinerary whole: Quad in Manila on Tuesday, a state visit on Wednesday, Shenzhen on Thursday

The President is set to depart Washington early Monday for a diplomatic tour of the Philippines and China. As per a White House assistant press secretary, Ms. Wales, the trip includes a Quad leaders’ summit in Manila on Tuesday, November 17, followed by a first-ever trilateral meeting with President Xi and President Putin in Shenzhen on Thursday, November 19. The President is due to arrive in Manila on Tuesday evening local time to meet the leaders of India, Japan and Australia on the sidelines of the ASEAN summit. Following the Quad meeting, he is expected to sign a trade deal with Thailand and attend a special United States-ASEAN summit before joining a dinner hosted for ASEAN and other regional leaders. On Wednesday he will receive a state visit welcome at the presidential palace, followed by bilateral talks and a lunch banquet with the Philippine President. He will subsequently travel to Shenzhen to attend the APEC leaders’ dinner and meeting, and on Thursday is scheduled to hold bilateral talks and a working lunch with President Xi before concluding the visit with the trilateral meeting.

Subjective
StockBiz — the spokesman on force absent an agreement, and Mr. Kushner’s post on expanding the next round to Europe

The Kremlin spokesperson, Mr. Peskov, said Russia would use force to achieve its goals if it could not reach a security agreement with Europe. In an interview with domestic media on November 15, he said discussions on resolving the Ukraine conflict and establishing a security architecture in Europe would be meaningless without genuine efforts to seek peace. Earlier, speaking to the TASS news agency, he said European negotiators had not yet sought to contact Russia. Trilateral talks between Russia, the United States and Ukraine concluded on November 11 in Abu Dhabi, but no agreements were announced on a ceasefire, territorial disputes or long-term security guarantees. An American envoy, Mr. Kushner, said in a social media post over the weekend that Russia and Ukraine had agreed to expand participation in the next round of talks to include European partners.

Subjective
ProfiloPolitics — ‘two component parts, and neither can exist without the other,’ and a channel that waits for a call

The Kremlin warned on Sunday that Russia will achieve its goals in Ukraine by force if Europe leaves no room for negotiation, the spokesman tying any settlement of the war to a new security architecture for the whole continent and saying talks are pointless unless Europe genuinely wants peace. The spokesman’s words to a Vesti correspondent: ‘It is obvious that, one way or another, the settlement in Ukraine will be linked to a new security architecture on the European continent. These are two component parts, and neither can exist without the other.’ He also noted that the negotiators Europe has chosen have not yet attempted to make contact with Russia. The sequence is set out: the trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi ended on Wednesday with no agreement; on Friday, Europe’s leaders agreed to send a five-country team—Britain, France, Germany, Italy and Poland, alongside Union officials—into the process Mr. Kushner is brokering. Europe’s stated position, from the Council President, Mr. Costa, is that ‘only Ukraine has the legitimacy to decide on matters concerning its territory and sovereignty.’ Mr. Kushner announced on Saturday that the focus of the diplomacy is now on bringing Moscow and Europe into direct engagement and on preparing the agenda for the next round of trilateral talks. No date, venue or format for direct Europe-to-Russia talks has been announced. What happens next is a phone call: whether Europe’s team picks up the channel Mr. Kushner has opened, and what Moscow does if it does not.

Subjective
Valcore News — Ms. Peltola past 50 percent on the dashboard count, her rival waiting for every vote, and counting to Wednesday

Democrat Mary Peltola has claimed victory in Alaska’s Senate race, the only contest of the midterms still without a projected winner. After Saturday’s count she leads Senator Dan Sullivan by more than 11,000 votes and has nudged just past the 50 percent that would spare her a ranked-choice count; Senator Sullivan’s team says it is waiting for every vote, and counting runs to Wednesday, Alaska time. With more than 283,000 ballots counted and write-in votes shared out, Ms. Peltola has 50.1 percent of first-choice votes to Senator Sullivan’s 46.1 percent, a lead of more than 11,000. No winner has been formally projected. Even if she slips back under 50 percent, the ranked-choice tabulation is expected to favour her on the preferences counted so far. A victory would give the Democrats a 56-to-44 Senate majority from January, still short of the 60 votes needed to beat a filibuster. Her campaign declares victory, saying there is no mathematical path for her rival. Senator Sullivan’s spokesman, Mr. Adams, said the campaign was ‘still waiting for every ballot to be counted.’ The Division of Elections will keep counting through Wednesday, the last day it accepts absentee ballots mailed from overseas, followed by ranked-choice tabulation if no one has a majority.

Subjective
Fish4News — why 49.94 and 50.1 are the same count: the denominator, the 872 write-ins, and 157 votes

Ms. Peltola remains ahead in Alaska’s unresolved Senate election, with one set of figures placing her just below 50 percent and another displaying slightly more than 50 percent. The difference comes largely from how write-in votes are included in the calculation, not from two competing vote counts. The figures are from the state’s November 14 unofficial first-choice update, checked on Monday, November 16, 2026: Ms. Peltola 140,637 first-choice votes, 49.94 percent with write-ins counted; Senator Sullivan 129,424, 45.96 percent; Mr. Daniel J. Sullivan Jr. 4,652, 1.65 percent; and write-in votes 872, 0.31 percent, on 281,587 votes. Ms. Peltola leads the incumbent by 11,213 first-choice votes. The state’s complete summary includes the 872 write-in votes among 281,587; divided that way, her share is 49.94 percent. A separate display excludes those 872 unresolved write-ins from its calculation, leaving 280,715 votes in the denominator, and divided that way her share is approximately 50.1 percent; her underlying vote count is unchanged. On the full denominator she stands 157 votes short of the majority threshold. The results portal is still marked unofficial, and ranked-choice tabulation is scheduled for Wednesday, November 18, if necessary.

Subjective
Korea JoongAng Daily — Mr. Huang seeks a return four days after resigning, and the petition passes 160,000

Days after resigning as Nvidia’s chief, Mr. Huang is reportedly weighing a comeback, with major investors urging the board to consider reinstating him and petitions from employees and shareholders gathering momentum. Mr. Huang has discussed ways to reclaim the post with close associates, a British newspaper reported on Sunday, citing multiple sources. Calls for his return are spreading inside and outside the company: more than 160,000 people have signed an online petition titled ‘Stand With Jensen.’ The chiefs of Tesla and SpaceX, Epic Games, Y Combinator and a co-founder of Cohere have publicly backed it. Two major shareholders—the chief of Altimeter Capital and the founder of Atreides Management—sent letters to the board urging it to consider all options, including Mr. Huang’s return. The Treasury Secretary also called for a sweeping overhaul at the company on Sunday. The company is trying to limit uncertainty from the leadership gap ahead of its fiscal third quarter earnings release on Tuesday.
